title: Research on the modeling method of unsteady aerodynamics for composite configuration based on the physics-embedded long short-term memory neural network
abstract: To address the aerodynamic modeling challenges posed by strong nonlinearities and hysteresis effects in high-angle-of-attack maneuvers, this study takes the prepositive elliptical wing-main wing composite flow control configuration as the research object. A method is proposed that explicitly embeds physical information into a conditional long short-term memory neural network for aerodynamic parameter identification and unsteady aerodynamic model construction. Taking the improved unsteady aerodynamic state-space equation of the composite configuration as the prior physical constraint, the conditional long short-term memory neural network is synchronously introduced to capture the temporal dependence relationship. The outputs of the two branches are dynamically fused through learnable weights to achieve the collaborative optimization of physical consistency and data fidelity. Taking the two-dimensional prepositive elliptical wing-main wing composite configuration as the research object, the neural network is trained and tested based on the dataset generated by computational fluid dynamics that covers multiple design parameters and working conditions. The results show that the root mean squared error of the intelligent modeling method proposed in this paper is reduced by more than 45% and 47% on the training set and the validation set respectively compared with the traditional single model. When verifying the generalization ability, whether for interpolation or extrapolation, the correlation coefficients of the aerodynamic coefficient prediction are all better than 0.999, and the average relative error is reduced by more than 20%. This framework combines physical interpretability and data adaptability, providing a new interpretable and transferable paradigm for the high-precision prediction of unsteady aerodynamics in complex flow environments.

title: Few-shot anomaly detection for aerospace telemetry data based on model-agnostic meta-learning
abstract: This paper addresses the deep learning-based telemetry data anomaly detection for spacecraft under few-shot conditions. The deficiency of the anomaly samples is one of the main challenges for deep learning-based anomaly detection. To tackle this issue, we propose a model-agnostic - meta-learning (MAML) approach for anomaly detection. We first train a baseline detection model based on long-short term memory network (LSTM) under few-shot conditions and detect the anomalies by the error threshold. To improve the detection model when facing few-shot conditions, we incorporate the MAML into the baseline model. During the process, we first directly introduce the MAML framework to the baseline model, and the evaluation indicators are improved. Then, to obtain higher precision, we introduce the multi-step loss optimization and geometric adaptive preprocessor to the standard MAML. The proposed method is verified on mars science laboratory (MSL) dataset from NASA, and the results demonstrate that our approach achieves high-precision anomaly detection under few-shot conditions compared with the state-of-the-art time-series anomaly detection model.

title: A physics-informed graph attention network with sparse temporal block selection for aircraft hydraulic system fault diagnosis
abstract: Precise fault diagnosis of aircraft hydraulic systems is critical to ensuring flight safety. However, conventional methods are often topology-agnostic, failing to leverage physical constraints, while standard graph-based models struggle with the computational burden and information dilution inherent in ultra-long time-series. This paper proposes the Topology-Aware Block-Sparse Graph Attention Network (TABS-GATNet), a physics-informed hierarchical framework that incorporates an efficient sparse temporal block selection mechanism. The framework embeds physical knowledge by constructing a spatio-temporal graph that explicitly mirrors the system's component topology and dynamic connections. To address the challenge of long sequences, TABS-GATNet deploys an attention-guided block-sparse selection mechanism. It formulates a novel block-scoring criterion by fusing global and local attention statistics to adaptively identify the most salient temporal blocks. The model then adopts a coarse-to-fine strategy, performing fine-grained feature extraction exclusively on these blocks and integrating the resulting features with the coarse representation through a gated mechanism for final diagnosis. Evaluated on a high-fidelity simulation dataset of an aircraft hydraulic system, the proposed TABS-GATNet achieves 99.01% diagnostic accuracy, demonstrating significant improvements over conventional benchmarks. Furthermore, ablation studies and attention visualizations validate the efficacy of the sparse mechanism and confirm that the model's diagnostic decisions align with the system's physical fault mechanisms, establishing a trustworthy and effective solution.

title: Aircraft engine performance prediction via a physics-informed two-stage network framework
abstract: Digital twin technology has become increasingly important in aero-engine performance analysis and virtual testing through data-driven modeling, but the limitations of black-box models pose significant challenges for safety-critical applications. This study proposes a physics-informed two-stage network framework for engine performance prediction, in which key engine state parameters are implicitly embedded through a stage-wise training strategy, thereby reducing the reliance on internal measurements during inference. Once trained, the model can efficiently predict engine performance using only ambient temperature, ambient pressure, and power lever angle. Furthermore, a graph neural network is introduced to explicitly encode the engine’s physical structural topology, and dynamic adjacency matrices are employed under different operating conditions to model the coupling relationships among engine components, enhancing model interpretability and enabling more accurate characterization of the engine’s complex internal interactions. Validation on a real engine test dataset demonstrated that the proposed method achieves high accuracy and strong robustness in predicting thrust, high-pressure compressor outlet pressure and exhaust gas temperature. In actual physical units, the maximum mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) for all performance parameters is 2.63%, and the maximum root mean square percentage error (RMSPE) is 4.65%.

title: Physics-informed neural network-based robust model predictive control for free-floating space robots
abstract: This paper presents a computationally efficient and disturbance-resilient real-time control framework for free-floating space robots (FFSRs), targeting joint tracking errors ≤ 0.1 rad, disturbance rejection efficiency ≥ 70%, and an average per-cycle computation time ≤ 0.01 s for a 6-DOF FFSR. The framework combines Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) with a disturbance-compensated Model Predictive Controller (MPC) to achieve high-precision tracking and suppression of base-attitude disturbances under real-time constraints. A PINN-based modeling approach is developed to capture the nonlinear, time-varying dynamics of FFSRs while embedding physical constraints into the learning process, thereby improving model fidelity with reduced data dependency. To enhance robustness against model uncertainties and external disturbances, a Linear Extended State Observer (LESO) is incorporated into the MPC architecture for real-time disturbance estimation and feedforward compensation. Simulation studies on a 6-DOF FFSR show that, under bounded disturbances and actuator constraints, the proposed method outperforms the LPV-MPC and PINN-MPC baselines in tracking accuracy, disturbance rejection, and base-disturbance suppression; in particular, it reduces the tracking MSE by 91.4% relative to LPV-MPC. Moreover, under the same hardware and software conditions, the proposed method reduces the average online per-cycle computation time by 99.9% relative to LPV-MPC, while keeping the mean computation time below the control sampling period, thereby supporting potential real-time feasibility.

title: Modeling and analysis of free vibration and supersonic flutter in metamaterial sandwich structures for aerospace applications: Verification of results using a hybrid machine learning algorithm
abstract: This study investigates the free vibration and supersonic flutter characteristics of metamaterial sandwich structures for aerospace applications, particularly focusing on a sandwich doubly curved panel with origami-enabled auxetic metamaterial face sheets and an auxetic lattice core. The panel's unique auxetic re-entrant unit cell geometry significantly influences its dynamic behavior. A hybrid machine learning algorithm is employed to verify the results, combining the computational efficiency of traditional methods with data-driven predictive capabilities. The Carrera’s unified formulation (CUF) with virtual displacements is adopted to model the structural response, accounting for complex geometries and varying material properties. For the aerodynamic modeling, the first-order piston theory is applied to simulate supersonic aerodynamic pressures, while the third-order piston theory is utilized for hypersonic flow conditions. To solve the governing equations, CUF-based models are constructed using Legendre polynomials, allowing for a precise and flexible representation of the panel's deformations under dynamic loading. Additionally, an analytical solution methodology is developed using double Fourier-based expansions to handle the complexity of the sandwich structure's dynamic and aerodynamic interactions. The study’s results provide a comprehensive understanding of the vibration and flutter behavior of metamaterial sandwich panels, offering valuable insights for the design of advanced aerospace structures subjected to supersonic and hypersonic flow regimes. The hybrid machine learning approach effectively enhances the predictive accuracy and reliability of the proposed models, making it a promising tool for future aerospace engineering applications.

title: Modelling and quantifying numerical integration errors in deep reinforcement learning for propulsion dynamics
abstract: This study investigates how numerical integration accuracy influences the training dynamics and control performance of deep reinforcement learning controllers applied to propulsion system simulations. The propulsion dynamics are represented by a continuous second-order thrust-driven model that is discretised using four numerical integration configurations: Euler (coarse, medium, and fine time steps) and Runge-Kutta fourth order (RK4). Three widely used model-free reinforcement learning algorithms, Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO), Soft Actor-Critic (SAC), and Twin Delayed Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (TD3), are evaluated together with a linear proportional-derivative baseline controller. A large experimental campaign comprising more than 50,000 simulated episodes was conducted across three training phases to quantify the influence of discretisation accuracy on reward convergence, trajectory stability, and control energy. The results demonstrate that numerical integration fidelity significantly shapes the optimisation landscape experienced by reinforcement learning agents. Under coarse Euler discretisation, PPO exhibits unstable learning behaviour and large oscillatory trajectories, while SAC maintains improved robustness but still shows sensitivity to large time steps. TD3 demonstrates the highest tolerance to discretisation error, maintaining stable closed-loop dynamics even under coarse integration. Higher-accuracy numerical schemes substantially improve learning efficiency. The RK4 configuration produces smoother trajectories, reduced control energy, and faster convergence across all reinforcement learning algorithms. Quantitative analysis of trajectory stability, integrated error metrics, and reward statistics confirms that discretisation error directly propagates through the learning process and alters the resulting control policies. These findings provide new empirical evidence that numerical integration fidelity is a critical design factor for reinforcement learning environments involving dynamical systems. The study highlights the necessity of carefully selecting integration schemes when training reinforcement learning controllers for propulsion dynamics and other physics-based control applications.

title: Telemetry-driven physics-informed prediction for on-orbit thermal–electrical performance of solar panels in satellite power system
abstract: For small satellites and CubeSat missions, body-mounted solar panels serve as the primary and often sole source of onboard power. Accurate prediction of the on-orbit thermal–electrical performance of small satellite solar panels is critical for power system management and health monitoring. However, it remains challenging due to complex orbital environments, unstable attitude motion, and limited availability of high-fidelity telemetry information. This paper proposes a physics-informed machine learning (PIML) prediction model for satellite solar panels under uncertain orbital environment conditions. The proposed approach avoids reliance on detailed flight information by converting measured telemetry into physically admissible information. A telemetry-driven orbital environment inversion strategy is developed to infer the solar panel’s thermal environment from real-time telemetry data. Based on the equivalent environmental states, a thermal–electrical soft constraint model is constructed to define a limiting scope of operation. The resulting physics-informed constraints are fused with telemetry data and used as hybrid inputs to PIML prediction models, encoded by recurrent neural networks (RNN) and long short-term memory networks (LSTM). The prediction model is evaluated using real-time telemetry from the TURUS satellite. Multiple prediction scenarios are designed, and the results demonstrate that the PIML prediction model is stable, physical consistent, and generalized. This study provides a practical solution for on-orbit thermal–electrical performance prediction under telemetry-limited conditions.

title: Conditional physics-informed deep operator networks for low earth orbit satellite trajectory prediction
abstract: With the deployment of large-scale constellations, accurate orbit prediction for Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellites is critical for space situational awareness. The increasing complexity of these mega-constellations also imposes significant challenges on dynamic topology management [1] and inter-satellite routing [2], where precise orbital information serves as a fundamental prerequisite. The standard SGP4 model has limited accuracy, while purely data-driven methods often lack physical consistency and generalization capabilities. To address this challenge, this paper proposes a prediction framework based on a Conditional Physics-Informed Deep Operator Network (Conditional PI-DeepONet). The model utilizes the DeepONet architecture to learn a general operator that maps a satellite’s initial conditions to its full state trajectory, enabling flexible predictions from any given epoch. By incorporating the governing orbital dynamics-including central gravity, J2 perturbation, and atmospheric drag-as a soft constraint in the loss function, the framework ensures the physical self-consistency of the predictions. Furthermore, a system reduction technique is employed to enhance training stability. Based on a high-quality dataset with ground truth labels from the International Laser Ranging Service (ILRS), we conduct comprehensive experiments in both single-satellite and multi-satellite scenarios. The results demonstrate that the proposed PINN model significantly outperforms SGP4 and a data-only baseline model in terms of prediction accuracy. This study validates the effectiveness of the proposed framework as a high-precision, flexible tool for LEO orbit prediction.

title: A physics-informed sparse coding framework for reconstruction of multiple impulsive maneuvers
abstract: Characterizing the motion of non-cooperative space objects is essential for space situational awareness, yet traditional orbit determination often fails when unknown maneuvers occur. Precisely maintaining orbital custody and ensuring collision safety require accurate, efficient reconstruction of these impulsive maneuvers. However, existing methods struggle to simultaneously reconstruct the timing, magnitude, and direction of multiple impulsive maneuvers with low computational effort. This paper proposes a physics-informed sparse coding framework that integrates physical dynamics and sparse coding techniques to reconstruct multiple unknown impulsive maneuvers from tracking data. This method models thrust as a temporally group-sparse exogenous input and integrates high-fidelity dynamics with measurements in an efficient batch projected formulation, which significantly reduces the computational burden while maintaining reconstruction accuracy. A projection step analytically eliminates the initial-state uncertainty, yielding a reduced thrust-only convex problem. The maneuver reconstructions can be obtained from solving this problem through group-sparsity-aware optimization techniques. Numerical simulations indicate that the proposed method accurately reconstructs multiple impulsive maneuvers in high-fidelity scenarios, including low Earth, medium Earth, highly elliptical orbits, and several real-world cases. These results demonstrate the adaptability of the proposed framework to realistic operating conditions, positioning the framework as a powerful tool for maneuver inference and intent characterization in realistic operational scenarios.

title: Data-efficient neural operator surrogates for nonlinear pitch dynamics of blunt-body re-entry vehicles
abstract: Accurate prediction of blunt body pitch dynamics during atmospheric entry is challenged by nonlinear aerodynamics, experimental limitations, and the prohibitive cost of free-flight CFD (FF-CFD). Previous FF-CFD-based system identification and Bayesian inference approaches using Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) are computationally intensive, data-hungry, and sensitive to prior knowledge. To address these limitations, a neural ordinary differential equation (neural ODE) surrogate is developed to learn continuous-time pitching dynamics directly from trajectory data. The study is carried out in two phases at Mach 1.44 using simulated free-flight data of ballistic-range experiments of the Genesis sample return capsule. The first phase consists of a synthetic study, where controlled trajectory data are used to evaluate the extrapolation and generalization behavior. Training on a single initial condition with short time windows of 0.7s extrapolated accurately to 1.4s, whereas training on multiple initial conditions at angles-of-attack of 1∘ and 20∘ generalized across the 1∘-40∘ range. The reconstructed dynamic stability coefficient agrees with MCMC benchmarks, demonstrating accurate recovery of nonlinear stability behavior. In the second phase, FF-CFD simulations were conducted using initial angles-of-attack 1∘ and 20∘ for training and 2∘, 5∘, 10∘, and 30∘ for validation. The neural ODE reproduces oscillatory responses with an approximately 1∘ error, generalizes to both the in- and out-of-distribution regimes, and provides calibrated uncertainty bands with variational inference. Compared to MCMC-based inverse estimation, the proposed neural ODE approach achieves higher predictive accuracy. These results demonstrate that neural ODE surrogates offer a data-efficient, uncertainty-aware, and scalable framework for re-entry vehicle stability analysis.

title: Hybrid Aero-PINN: A physics-consistent deep learning framework for efficient aerodynamic prediction
abstract:
Aerodynamic prediction across various operating conditions is a major challenge for data-driven models. They often struggle with limited generalisation, poor physical consistency, and excessive reliance on large datasets. This work introduces a Hybrid Aero-Physics-Informed Neural Network (Hybrid Aero-PINN) that integrates machine learning with aerodynamic theory to address these issues. The term physics-informed is used here in a structured, neuro-symbolic sense, where physical consistency is enforced through deterministic analytical operators rather than soft constraint enforcement of governing equations. Instead of treating finite-wing aerodynamics as a black-box problem, our framework decomposes the physics into two regimes. A deep neural network is trained to predict two-dimensional viscous airfoil coefficients from angle of attack, Reynolds number, camber, and thickness. This captures nonlinear boundary-layer and separation effects. The network's outputs then pass through a physics layer that analytically integrates the results to calculate three-dimensional lift, drag, and the lift-to-drag ratio using established aerodynamic principles. The author generates a high-quality dataset using XFOIL in a controlled pre-stall regime. The author rigorously filters this dataset using linearity, Reynolds scaling, and aspect ratio constraints to remove physically unstable samples. For benchmarking, a purely data-driven black-box neural network trained on the same dataset produces RMSE(L/D) = 0.966 and R² = 0.972 (L/D MAPE = 2.43%). The Hybrid Aero-PINN attains R²(L/D) = 0.9818 and L/D MAPE = 1.84% (sectional: R²(

title: Physics-informed transformer with residual analysis and adaptive threshold Kalman filter for angle-of-attack sensor fault detection
abstract: The angle-of-attack (AoA) sensor is essential to modern aircraft systems; however, its vulnerability to faults has contributed to several aviation accidents. This study proposes two novel sensor fusion-based fault detection methods that combine data-driven techniques with physics principles: the Physics-Informed Transformer with Residual Analysis (PITRA) and the Adaptive Threshold Kalman Filter (ATKF). PITRA uses a physics-informed encoder-decoder transformer to construct a virtual AoA sensor. By incorporating reduced-order aircraft dynamics into the loss function and applying an adaptive weight (γadaptive) to balance physics-informed and data-driven losses, PITRA enhances AoA estimation. The ATKF augments a reduced-order aircraft model with sensor bias and gain parameters for fault detection using adaptive thresholding and Kalman filtering. Both methods are evaluated using using flight data from the Advanced Technologies Testing Aircraft System (ATTAS) under fault-free, faulty, and noisy sensor conditions. Sensitivity analyses with Gaussian and non-Gaussian sensor noise showed that PITRA (γadaptive) is more robust in noisy environments. During elevator maneuver with a 10% Gaussian noise-to-signal power ratio (NSPR) AoA sensor, PITRA achieved an average false positive rate (FPR) of 0, compared to 12.8 ± 19.8 for ATKF. PITRA (γadaptive, Noisy), trained on 70% of the dataset with 10% NSPR Gaussian noise, performed better with only minimal degradation. However, ATKF outperformed PITRA in terms of detection delay, identifying ramp faults in 0.18 seconds, compared to 0.44 seconds. The research shows that while physics-informed machine learning models require significant computational resources, they excel in noisy environments. In contrast, physics-based fault detection methods using Kalman filters are less resource-intensive and more effective.

title: PHD-NO: A physics-guided hash-encoding dual-branch neural operator for transonic supercritical airfoil aerodynamics
abstract:
Supercritical airfoils operating in transonic flows present an inherent multiscale challenge, where sharp shock discontinuities are coupled with delicate, attached boundary layer structures. Conventional neural operators often suffer from inherent spectral bias, where global smooth features are prioritized over high-frequency singularities or encounter non-physical Gibbs oscillations when attempting to resolve shocks via global encodings. To address this limitation, we propose the physics-guided hash-encoding dual-branch neural operator (PHD-NO). Its central design is a dual-branch hash-encoding architecture tailored to transonic aerodynamic fields, where the background flow and shock-dominated corrections are handled in a scale-decoupled manner. By employing multi-resolution hash grid encoding as a unified feature basis, the framework leverages the locally compact support of fine-resolution grids to achieve exceptional spatial precision at shock locations while maintaining global consistency through coarse-resolution levels. Theoretically, we analyze PHD-NO through the Neural Tangent Kernel framework and argue that the multi-scale hash sub-kernels can compensate for high-frequency eigenvalue decay over a broader frequency range, thereby mitigating the spectral-bias gap. On a high-fidelity supercritical-airfoil dataset, PHD-NO attains mean L1 errors at the 
10
−
3

title: Simulating and analyzing the flow field of an oscillating airfoil via physics-informed neural networks with data assimilation
abstract: Research on unsteady flow field of oscillating airfoil is closely related to the methods of handling turbulence problems. Experimental measurements and numerical simulations, both of which have their own limitations-high cost or inability to simultaneously achieve computational accuracy and efficiency. In this work, we proposed a physics-informed neural network model based on data assimilation (DA-PINN) to simulate and analyze the flow field of the National Advisory Committee for Aeronautics(NACA)0015 airfoil during pitching oscillation. The entire construction process is as follows: 1/ Establish a machine learning model based on physical constraints, with training data obtained from Reynolds-Averaged Navier-Stokes(RANS) numerical simulation; 2/ Obtain oscillating airfoil flow field data under experimental conditions through wind tunnel experiments; 3/ On the basis of the above machine learning model, add an experimental data assimilation constraint term to further optimize the training model. Through comparison, we found that the model constructed using data assimilation technology has higher accuracy and can accurately simulate the oscillating airfoil flow field. This data assimilation model has a wide range of applications.

title: Application of optically enhanced technique-assisted cascaded neural networks to hydrogen extreme combustion flow field reconstruction
abstract: Accurate sensing and prediction of combustion flow dynamics are critical factors for ensuring the reliable operation of scramjet engines under complex operating conditions. Traditional deep learning techniques often neglect the critical optical atomization effects in supersonic combustion flow field reconstruction, resulting in poor visual quality of the reconstructed flow fields. This paper conducts a ground experimental study of a scramjet engine with hydrogen injection pressures of 2 MPa, 3 MPa, and 4 MPa under Ma=3.0 conditions. We propose an Optically Enhanced Cascaded Neural Network (OECNN) assisted by optical enhancement techniques. The method first employs an Encoder-Decoder network for preliminary high-dimensional feature abstraction and compression, followed by the LiteDehazeNet to integrate the extracted features and enhance optical clarity, ultimately generating predicted schlieren images. Finally, a comparative analysis is conducted with the commonly used models Chens, Kongs, and UNet. Experimental results demonstrate that the OECNN model achieves maximum improvements of 56.48% in Peak Signal-to-Noise Ratio (PSNR), 28.33% in Structural Similarity Index Measure (SSIM), and 2.77% in correlation coefficient (R) compared to the other three models. The OECNN achieves an optimal balance between model complexity and accuracy. Compared with existing models, it reduces parameter count by up to 93.54% (merely 41.6 MB), demonstrating the effectiveness of its lightweight design and flow field reconstruction capability.

title: Deep-learning of satellite aerodynamics in very low Earth orbit with partial-physics pretraining
abstract: In very low Earth orbits (VLEOs), orbital decay induced by atmospheric drag is non-trivial, hence accurate aerodynamic models are required for reliable satellite design and mission planning. However, obtaining high-fidelity representations through whole-physics stochastic particle solvers, e.g., Direct Simulation Monte Carlo, for orbit propagation is generally out of reach for most modern computing systems. As such, a deep-learning framework is proposed for cost-effective surrogate modelling of satellite aerodynamics. Models are first pretrained in a cheap partial-physics environment to learn a theory-based component that serves as a baseline, i.e., Sentman’s closed-form solutions for theoretical flat panels. A correction term is then transfer-learned from sparse samples of the whole-physics, high-fidelity aerodynamics to restore the influence from the omitted physics. The models are deployed in several case studies including (i) validation against the GOCE satellite over a selected time window; (ii) orbit propagation of a conceptual satellite; (iii) design study on variation of surface properties. With transfer-learning, models are found to demonstrate improved generalizability and better interpretability according to gradient-based attribution metrics. Using only 14 whole-physics samples for transfer-learning, ground track errors in estimated trajectories obtained through orbit propagation over 20 days, were reduced by 85% as compared to using the partial-physics solver. Considering both offline and online compute costs, transfer-learning incurs up to only 0.87% of the total cost when using whole-physics solvers. By exploiting existing knowledge of partial-physics environments, a scalable and cost-efficient deep-learning framework is discovered for satellite aerodynamics in VLEO.

title: A two-stage physics-informed graph neural network approach for rapid and accurate turbine blade temperature field prediction and data fusion
abstract: Accurate and rapid prediction of the temperature field on turbine blades is critical for the safety, performance, and lifespan of modern gas turbines. Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) and machine learning are two mainstream prediction methods. While CFD provides detailed thermal analysis, it suffers from high computational costs and inherent discrepancies with physical reality. Furthermore, traditional machine learning approaches are not suitable for unstructured meshes and lack physical interpretability. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a two-stage Physics-Informed Graph Neural Network (PIGNN) framework for precise turbine blade temperature prediction and data fusion. In the first stage, a physics embedded GNN model is developed to learn the complex mapping from boundary conditions to the steady-state temperature field across the blade’s unstructured mesh, which explicitly embeds the steady-state heat conduction mechanism into the message passing process of the graph neural network. In the second stage, the framework learns the deviation field between the previous PIGNN’s prediction and sparse, high-fidelity temperature measurements from experiments, effectively fusing the global information from CFD with the local accuracy of experimental data. Results demonstrate that the proposed two-stage PIGNN framework enables fast and accurate temperature field prediction, achieving prediction within 8 ms and the average relative error below 0.41%. Furthermore, when corrected by sparse experimental data, the model’s final prediction error is reduced by 83%. This work presents both a novel PIGNN method for rapid thermal prediction and a robust paradigm for fusing multi-source data to develop reliable digital twins.

title: A POD-DeepONet based parameter identification framework for the phenomenological model of liquid rocket engine combustion instability
abstract: The stability margin is a key indicator of the operational reliability of liquid rocket engines (LREs). Conventional assessment approaches, such as parameter perturbation and external excitation, often require lengthy testing cycles, incur high costs, and provide limited mechanistic insight, thereby limiting efficient quantitative evaluation of stability characteristics under design-relevant conditions. Recent parameter identification methods based on phenomenological models offer a promising alternative by inferring stability parameters directly from pressure oscillation data. However, these models are formulated as stochastic differential equations, and their identification typically requires solving the inverse problem of the adjoint Fokker–Planck equation (AFP), which involves computationally intensive numerical iterations. To address this challenge, this study develops a POD-DeepONet-based surrogate approach that integrates Proper Orthogonal Decomposition with Deep Operator Networks. By using POD bases extracted from the AFP solution space as a fixed output representation, the framework learns the mapping from phenomenological parameters to finite-time Kramers–Moyal coefficient fields. Results show that POD-DeepONet improves offline training efficiency by 5.2 times and achieves a 2600-fold acceleration in online identification in the tested cases, while maintaining accuracy comparable to the finite-difference method. These results demonstrate its potential for computationally efficient stability-related parameter identification in LRE-oriented phenomenological modeling.

title: Physics-informed digital twin for spacecraft structures under sensor faults: Virtual sensing via a frequency attention U-Net and closed-loop model updating
abstract: Verification and validation (V&V) of structural digital twins becomes fragile when high-frequency Sim-to-Real mismatch coexists with sensor-fault-induced under-observability, as missing channels undermine reliable diagnosis and model updating. To improve trustworthy V&V under partial observation, we present a physics-informed virtual sensing and closed-loop updating framework that reconstructs masked frequency responses and enables stable constrained FEM-parameter updating. Specifically, we couple a reduced-order FEM (ROM) prior with a Frequency Attention U-Net (FAU) that injects Fourier Neural Operator (FNO) global spectral increments through Transformer-gated fusion, driving constrained parameter updating. Systematic experiments on a scaled reconfigurable spacecraft across multiple geometric configurations and two excitation conditions, 10 Hz and 800 Hz, validate the framework’s efficacy. Under 800 Hz excitation, the proposed virtual sensing reduces the log-amplitude main-peak error metric by an average of 76.7 dB under the adopted full-spectrum peak-search protocol. Furthermore, in missing-channel scenarios, the closed-loop updating strategy robustly limits log-amplitude errors on masked channels to 8–10 dB, outperforming spatial interpolation baselines (up to 48 dB error). These improvements reconstruct reliable full-field spectra, supporting physics-consistent interpretation of configuration-dependent joint softening through effective ROM-level parameter trends and providing a foundation for proactive diagnosis and smart maintenance.

title: High-fidelity aerodynamic prediction via a physics-informed transformer framework
abstract: Accurate prediction of aerodynamic coefficients for systems with strongly coupled and nonlinear dynamics, such as microspoiler-controlled vehicles, remains challenging in aerospace engineering. Purely data-driven models often lack physical consistency, while classical Physics-Informed Neural Networks are difficult to apply directly to complex three-dimensional aerodynamic flows. This paper proposes the Aero Physics-Informed Network, a data-assisted physics-guided surrogate framework for aerodynamic coefficient prediction. The framework first constructs physically meaningful aerodynamic descriptors from raw operating parameters through physics-guided feature engineering, thereby improving the physical relevance of the input representation without direct PDE-residual optimization. These features are then processed by an Ensemble Kalman Filter-based Physics-Informed Attention mechanism, which refines feature weighting through physically guided updates during learning. The proposed model is trained on high-fidelity CFD data benchmarked against wind tunnel measurements. Comparative, ablation, and robustness studies show that APINN achieves improved predictive accuracy and maintains stronger performance than conventional deep learning baselines under noisy, sparse, and perturbed data conditions. These results indicate that embedding aerodynamic prior knowledge into both feature construction and attention refinement provides an effective and robust surrogate modeling strategy for complex aerodynamic prediction tasks.

title: Fourier feature embedded domain-decomposition physics-informed neural network impedance inversion approach for combustion chamber acoustic boundaries considering mean flow effects
abstract: Acoustic simulations of combustion chambers often exhibit uncertainty due to insufficient understanding of impedance boundary conditions. Recently, the physics-informed neural network (PINN)-based impedance inversion method has been proposed, replacing forward models with data-driven frameworks and breaking the iterative input parameter adjustment cycle of traditional optimization inversion approaches for matching simulated and observational data. However, applying this method to complex combustion chamber acoustic problems presents multiple challenges: complex geometries, heterogeneous acoustic fields, and difficulties in acquiring global training data. In particular, when the influence of mean flow inside the combustion chamber is taken into account, the complexity of the acoustic field increases significantly. Furthermore, direct measurement of velocity perturbations under practical operating conditions is infeasible, which further exacerbates the difficulty in solving impedance inversion problems. Additionally, a single network architecture with unified hyperparameters set struggles to simultaneously capture low and high frequency acoustic field characteristics, preventing stable frequency-independent solutions. To address this, this paper proposes a cross-frequency impedance inversion method based on domain decomposition physics-informed neural networks and Fourier feature embedding, tailored for complex combustion chamber acoustic boundary inversion problems considering the mean flow effect. Case studies conducted impedance inversion on combustion chamber inlet/outlet boundaries considering mean flow effect within the 20–3000 Hz range, where combustion noise is concentrated. Results show the method effectively captures acoustic characteristics even for complex models considering mean flow effect and unknown velocity perturbations, achieving precise inversion of unknown boundary impedances across 20–3000 Hz and providing a viable solution for related engineering problems.

title: Physics-informed neural predictive formation control: A unified framework for safe multi-vehicle coordination
abstract: Multi-vehicle formation control in obstacle-rich environments requires simultaneous optimization of competing objectives including formation maintenance, collision avoidance, and energy efficiency. Existing approaches face two critical limitations: 1) high sensitivity to trade-off parameters, requiring scenario-specific manual tuning when balancing formation maintenance against collision avoidance, and 2) the inherent difficulty of simultaneously optimizing competing objectives, specifically the balance between maintaining formation cohesion and ensuring collision avoidance, which often destabilizes learning and degrades performance. This paper presents Physics-Informed Neural Predictive Formation Control (PINPFC), a unified framework integrating physics-informed neural networks, reinforcement learning, and model predictive control to address these challenges. The PINPFC architecture employs a multi-branch neural network embedding vehicle dynamics, safety constraints, and formation requirements as differentiable physics-informed loss functions, significantly mitigating the need for manual hyperparameter tuning by making competing objectives intrinsic to the network structure. A self-attention mechanism adaptively allocates control authority among branches by learning from real-time formation errors, safety violations, and physical consistency, while the MPC layer ensures hard constraint satisfaction and recursive feasibility. Theoretical analysis establishes formation convergence with explicit ultimate bounds, strict collision avoidance through hierarchical MPC-enforced constraints, and bounded suboptimality relative to centralized control. Comprehensive experimental validation across varying obstacle densities demonstrates that PINPFC achieves measurable improvements in strict success rates and near-collision rates compared to baseline methods, with performance advantages becoming increasingly pronounced in high-density scenarios.

title: A cross-configuration multi-fidelity framework for aerodynamic modeling: DeepONet with adaptive gated fusion and transfer learning
abstract: Accurate prediction of aerodynamic coefficients is essential for guiding aircraft design optimization and performance evaluation. However, existing multi-fidelity surrogate models are typically constrained to narrow geometric training distributions and rely on simplified fusion strategies that lack adaptive weighting. This inability to intelligently fuse heterogeneous fidelity data and extract universal shape-performance relationships causes dramatic performance degradation when evaluating novel configurations, severely limiting their applicability in diverse cross-configuration design scenarios. To address these challenges, we propose a cross-configuration multi-fidelity aerodynamic prediction framework termed DeepONet-GF-TL (Deep Operator Network with Adaptive Gated Fusion and Transfer Learning). The method employs the DeepONet operator architecture as its backbone to decouple geometric and flow-condition feature extraction; integrates an adaptive gated fusion module that dynamically evaluates local data reliability to optimally weight heterogeneous fidelity information across varying flow regimes; introduces a residual skip connection that directly routes raw inputs to the prediction layer, explicitly learning targeted corrections for complex physical mechanisms inherently absent in low-fidelity data; and incorporates a dual-pathway attention mechanism for refined feature representation. On this basis, a two-stage transfer learning strategy with a full-freeze mechanism enables robust cross-configuration generalization on scarce high-fidelity samples while preventing catastrophic forgetting of universal shape-performance mappings. Comprehensive evaluations on 11 subsonic-to-transonic airfoils demonstrate that the proposed DeepONet-GF-TL achieves lift and drag coefficient prediction R2 exceeding 0.995, reducing MAE by 1.7 to 4.6 times compared to three established multi-fidelity baselines(MFGPR, MFNN, and TLNN). Tests on the CACM three-dimensional civil transport aircraft model with 20-dimensional geometric variations confirm robust cross-configuration generalization by accurately predicting the highly nonlinear support interference increments. The proposed method achieves an interference R2 exceeding 0.953 for lift and 0.949 for drag across 450 unseen configurations. Moreover, the method achieves 3 to 4 orders of magnitude speedup over Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD). These results demonstrate that the proposed framework enables accurate and efficient aerodynamic coefficient prediction across diverse geometries, fidelity gap types, and flow conditions.

title: A method for reconstructing the line-of-sight pointing of remote sensing satellites using a multimodal neural network integrated with FBG sensor networks
abstract: On-orbit monitoring of line-of-sight (LOS) pointing deviation is crucial for improving the target positioning accuracy of geostationary orbit (GEO) satellites. However, it remains a challenging task. To address this problem, this paper proposes a LOS pointing monitoring method based on an Fiber Bragg Grating(FBG) sensor network and a multimodal neural network. By deploying the FBG sensor network on the remote sensing payload support structure, high-precision measurement of the temperature and strain fields is achieved. A CNN-Transformer cascade neural network is then used to predict variations in LOS pointing. Specifically, the Convolutional Neural Network(CNN) extracts high-dimensional features from the FBG spectrum at each sensor location, and the Transformer performs multimodal fusion of these spectral features with the structural strain and temperature fields data, thereby improving the accuracy of the LOS pointing deviation prediction. This study specifically targets quasi-static thermal deformations of GEO satellites, where the thermal environment changes slowly and dynamic effects are negligible. A simplified model of the support structure for remote sensing payloads was constructed, and simulation experiments were carried out. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method can effectively monitor LOS pointing deviations caused by micro-deformation of the payload support structure, achieving a prediction accuracy that exceeds 98.3 %. This study provides a promising approach for high-precision on-orbit monitoring quasi-static, thermally induced LOS pointing deviations in GEO satellites.

title: Physics-informed CNN–transformer pointer network for decision-stage task allocation of large-scale airborne electro-optical swarms
abstract: Large-scale task allocation is a key decision-stage problem for airborne electro-optical (EO) swarms performing cooperative sensing, regional search, and target-level monitoring. This problem is challenging because UAV–task assignment must simultaneously handle high-dimensional combinatorial search, EO sensing-geometry constraints, cooperative localization requirements, and low-latency assignment generation. This study develops a physics-informed cooperative allocation framework that incorporates EO range and field-of-view constraints, cooperative localization geometry, regional-search coverage, and target-level threat-aware monitoring. A wedge-product-based geometric metric is introduced to characterize dual-platform passive-localization uncertainty and provide a sensing-geometry-aware basis for UAV–task assignment. To solve the resulting variable-scale assignment problem, a CNN–Transformer Pointer Network (CT-PN) is proposed, where a CNN branch extracts local sequence-level features and a Transformer branch models global assignment dependencies across the mixed UAV–target sequence. Simulation results show that CT-PN achieves a favorable tradeoff between decision quality and computational efficiency. In a representative large-scale scenario with 35 UAVs, CT-PN reduces the average decision cost by 30.6% and 25.2% compared with DQN and LSTM-PN, respectively, while maintaining a 12.4% average cost gap relative to the best-performing Iterated Greedy heuristic with more than a 400-fold computational speedup. A post-assignment noisy-bearing localization evaluation further shows that CT-PN improves cooperative localization feasibility beyond the optimized decision cost. At an angular-noise standard deviation of 0.1° and an error tolerance of one spatial unit, CT-PN achieves valid-and-accurate localization rates of 80.75%, 88.20%, and 85.30% in the small-, medium-, and large-scale scenarios, compared with 25.29%, 54.86%, and 54.09% for LSTM-PN. These results indicate that CT-PN provides a low-latency learning-based task-allocation policy with improved post-assignment sensing feasibility relative to learning-based baselines, while retaining a performance gap relative to computationally expensive heuristic search.

title: A physics-informed constrained gated low-rank adaptation framework for remaining useful life prediction of aeroengines
abstract: Remaining useful life (RUL) prediction for aeroengines is a key to accurately monitoring health status. However, existing methods have generally failed to model RUL prediction from an integrated perspective that accounts for empirical degradation, state decoupling, and operating-condition analysis. Furthermore, a persistent challenge lies in balancing data-driven cross-domain adaptability with the physics consistency of mechanistic laws. A physics-informed constrained gated low-rank adaptation framework is proposed for cross-domain RUL prediction, in which domain knowledge is decomposed into three complementary components, namely black-box state knowledge, operating-condition contextual knowledge, and physical degradation knowledge. Specifically, an in-structure modulation mechanism is designed to inject black-box state knowledge into sequence representations, while operating-condition contextual knowledge and physical degradation knowledge are explicitly embedded into the backbone network via gating to achieve dynamic feature modulation. To enable parameter-efficient adaptation during knowledge disentanglement, a degradation-progress-gated low-rank adaptation mechanism is proposed, aiming to adapt to the target domain with a minimal number of trainable parameters. Also, a degradation-consistency constraint strategy based on gradient conflict awareness is designed to achieve bidirectional correction of both physical penalties and data loss. Experiments demonstrate that the proposed method achieves the best average performance across 12 tasks and exhibits more stable physics consistency on representative tasks.

title: Integration of Shapley additive explanations and genetic algorithms for physics-informed aerodynamic shape optimization
abstract: Aerodynamic shape optimization for aircraft design is constrained by the high cost of high-fidelity CFD evaluations and by the stochastic blindness of conventional genetic mutation operators. This study develops SHAP-GA, a physics-guided evolutionary framework that converts model interpretability into gene-level mutation guidance for airfoil design. A database of 750 airfoils is constructed by using the UIUC airfoil archive only as the initial geometry source; each profile is reconstructed with 12 CST coefficients and re-evaluated using a validated ANSYS Fluent workflow at Mach numbers (Ma) of 0.2, 0.4, and 0.6 and an angle of attack (α) of 4°. The resulting CFD-labeled data are used to train a DNN surrogate with a test MRE of 0.647%. SHAP values extracted from the surrogate are transformed into online mutation guidance through a fifth-order Feature-SHAP Fitting mechanism with O(1) query cost and a sparse Norm-ReLU activation that suppresses detrimental geometric states while amplifying beneficial ones. In the 12-dimensional airfoil problem, the positive SHAP-guided GA consistently reduces fitness evaluations and reaches a peak overall mean improvement rate (OMIR) of 16.07% in the high-subsonic Ma = 0.6 condition. Controlled benchmark diagnostics further show substantial convergence gains, including peak OMIR values of 69.70% on the Rosenbrock valley and 43.90% and 18.42% in 3D and 5D tests, respectively. The interpretation also reveals a physically consistent sensitivity migration: lower-surface coefficients control circulation and aft pressure recovery at Ma = 0.2 and 0.4, whereas upper-surface leading-edge coefficients dominate shock-wave mitigation at Ma = 0.6. These results establish a CFD-validated, interpretable optimization strategy for aerodynamic design.

title: Design, machine learning based optimization, experimental validation and numerical analysis for free vibration of multi-auxetic sandwich structures with porosity-dependent GPL-reinforced core
abstract: This research pioneers multi-auxetic design in sandwich beam/plate structures through convergent integration of graphene platelet-reinforced (GPLR) functionally graded auxetic foams and machine-learning-optimized carbon fiber reinforced polymer (CFRP) laminates. Triaxial thermocompression-fabricated GPLR-aluminum cores with experimental temperature-dependent properties interface with inverse-designed laminates to form hierarchical structures exhibiting triaxial negative Poisson's ratio control. Experimental-computational validation confirms unprecedented vibration suppression capabilities, including a maximum of 30.18% natural frequency enhancement over non-auxetic systems, significant nonlinear oscillation attenuation, and superior enhancement effect on functionally graded (FG)-O configuration. Critical parametric analyses reveal non-monotonic frequency dependence on core-to-facesheet ratios and thermal degradation. These multi-auxetic architectures demonstrate transformative potential for aerospace vibration-isolation systems requiring multi-dynamic load adaptability.

title: RaPhy-PINO: An FRF-embedded neural operator for resonance-dominant forced-response prediction in aero-engine rotating blade systems
abstract: Resonance-dominant forced response in aero-engine rotating blade systems is governed by narrow-band frequency response function (FRF) amplification, making repeated vibration-stress screening across excitation, damping, and operating variations computationally expensive. This work proposes RaPhy-PINO, an FRF-embedded neural operator for rapid prediction of peak alternating stress and normalized stress-pattern fields over fatigue-relevant high-risk nodes. A Rational Resonance Layer injects modal-rational FRF topology through speed-interpolated prestressed natural frequencies and damping-aware features, while a Fourier-feature trunk reconstructs localized hotspot gradients. Training labels are generated by a physics-consistent offline–online workflow that retains a reference prestressed spatial modal basis and updates the natural frequencies in the analytical FRF denominators by piecewise-linear interpolation over rotational speed. The method is verified on a controlled cantilever-plate benchmark and demonstrated on a representative fan-blade sector under prescribed non-axisymmetric multi-harmonic excitation. On the plate benchmark, RaPhy-PINO improves damping-shift generalization over physics-agnostic and capacity-matched baselines. On the fan-blade case, it predicts peak stress with 𝑅2=0⁢.9997, RMSE = 2.37 MPa, and MAPE = 0.35%, and reconstructs the selected high-risk field with mean 𝑅2=0.9974, RMSE = 0.60 MPa, and mean relative 𝐿2 error = 0.41%. Independent MSC Nastran SOL 108 direct harmonic-response verification over ten representative cases yields mean peak-stress deviations of 0.63% for MSUM and 1.52% for RaPhy-PINO relative to the full-order FE solutions. A 100,000-sample Monte Carlo study demonstrates its utility for rapid resonance-window uncertainty propagation and uncertainty-aware ranking.

title: Physics-informed graph neural networks for forecasting eVTOL-induced traffic state perturbations in real-world road networks
abstract: The anticipated large-scale operation of electric vertical take-off and landing (eVTOL) aircraft is expected to induce transient passenger flow shocks in the vicinity of vertiports, the propagation of which must be accurately predicted to enable proactive traffic management. To address the tendency of purely data-driven models to generate physically inconsistent predictions for such sparse shock events, a physics-informed graph temporal network (PI-GTN) is proposed. The framework is built around three complementary components: (1) the Lighthill-Whitham-Richards (LWR) conservation law is generalized to sensor graphs of arbitrary topology via the graph Laplacian operator, and a graph-based conservation residual is constructed; (2) a lightweight architecture with two graph convolutional layers, temporal average pooling, and only approximately 5000 parameters is adopted; and (3) a “physics residual” metric that does not rely on ground-truth labels is introduced to quantify the physical consistency of predictions. The conservation residual is jointly optimized with a data-fitting loss and a spatial smoothness regularizer, forcing the predictions to obey traffic wave propagation physics. Under the simulated conditions, experimental results indicate that PI-GTN reduces the physics residual by 91.2% and the global MAE by 29.5% relative to an LSTM baseline, while in single-feature scenarios the smoothness residual is lowered by approximately two orders of magnitude. The established benchmark and metric provide a reproducible platform and a new evaluation dimension for ground–air coupled traffic prediction.

title: Sparse-measurement-constrained full-field stress updating of simulation-trained neural operators for aerospace structures
abstract: Accurate full-field stress prediction for real aerospace load-bearing structures is challenging because finite element (FE) simulations provide dense but biased stress fields, whereas experimental measurements are reliable but sparse. This study proposes a sparse-measurement-constrained full-field stress updating framework for simulation-trained neural operators. A fixed-mesh Fourier neural operator is first trained on FE-generated von Mises stress fields to provide a simulation-informed full-field prior. Sparse sensor measurements are then used to diagnose structured simulation-to-reality discrepancies and guide lightweight updating without retraining the surrogate. For a single-rod component with load-level-dependent discrepancy, a gated affine update selectively corrects low-load errors while preserving reliable medium- and high-load predictions. For a double-rod connected component with spatially heterogeneous discrepancy, a regional inverse distance weighting update propagates sensor residuals to the full field according to structural topology. Validation on two aerospace engine-frame components shows that the proposed updates improve sensor-level consistency and preserve physically meaningful stress-field patterns. In leave-one-sensor-out validation, the Case-1 MAPE is reduced from 6.109% to 4.113%, and the Case-2 MAPE is reduced from 24.328% to 18.022%. The framework provides a practical route for measurement-constrained digital-twin stress evaluation under sparse sensing conditions.

title: ANO-MPFM: An Attention Neural Operator Framework for Multi-physics Collaborative Online Estimation of Integrated Ducted Fan-Motor Systems
abstract: The safe operation of integrated ducted fan-motor systems (DF-MSs) under complex operating conditions critically depends on precise characterization of their aerodynamic and thermal states. In practical scenarios highly constrained sensor placement, combined with the intricate coupling between aerodynamic and thermal states, renders this task particularly challenging. This study proposes an attention neural operator-based multi-physics framework (ANO-MPFM), which seamlessly integrates extensive simulation datasets with in-situ sensor measurements to reconstruct spatially non-uniform multi-physics fields and estimate key performance parameters of DF-MSs, offering enhanced interpretability. A collaborative reconstruction strategy is developed, whereby base field priors guide the accurate inference of complex fields. During this prior knowledge integration, a Galerkin attention block explicitly encodes long-range physical priors across domains. Applied to a representative DF-MS case, using only rotational speed and eight motor temperature measurements as observations, the proposed framework achieves outstanding reconstruction performance, with an overall mean absolute error below 8.93×10-3, an overall coefficient of determination exceeding 0.99, and minimal error fluctuations. The approach outperforms conventional models, particularly in reconstructing complex aerodynamic fields of the ducted fan. Further analysis examining the impact of observation noise and sensor placement indicates that temperature measurement points on the motor housing constitute the most critical sensitive regions influencing reconstruction accuracy. The present study offers valuable technical guidance for state monitoring and the design of robust control strategies for DF-MSs operating under complex environmental conditions.

title: Deep reinforcement learning-based double-layer coordinated output voltage prediction method for lithium battery in unmanned aerial vehicle applications
abstract: Under the dynamic flight conditions of hybrid electric unmanned aerial vehicles(UAVs), frequent fluctuations in demand power can cause pronounced variations in lithium battery output voltage, thereby posing challenges to energy management and flight safety. This study proposes a deep reinforcement learning-based double-layer coordinated output voltage prediction method(DRLDCPM) to improve prediction accuracy and response capability under the dynamic UAV flight conditions. The proposed method employs a double-layer coordinated prediction framework consisting of an upper temporal learning layer and a lower residual correction layer. In the upper layer, a long short-term memory network is employed as a base predictor to capture the time-varying characteristics of lithium battery and generate an initial voltage prediction. In the lower layer, a deep deterministic policy gradient algorithm is designed as a residual corrector to dynamically compensate for the prediction errors. The effectiveness and applicability of the proposed DRLDCPM are demonstrated through comparative experiments with recursive least squares(RLS), sequential quadratic programming(SQP), and long short-term memory-backpropagation neural network(LSTM-BP). Compared with RLS, SQP, and LSTM-BP, the proposed DRLDCPM reduces the mean absolute error by 28.1%, 18.9% and 13.6%, respectively, and the corresponding root mean square error by 32.4%, 30.2% and 18.0%, respectively. The proposed method provides more timely and reliable voltage prediction information, thereby supporting battery state monitoring, energy management, low-voltage warning, and flight safety assurance in hybrid-electric UAVs.

title: Multiphysics aeroelastic stability of axially moving functionally graded perovskite‑piezoelectric plates under yawed supersonic flow: A hybrid numerical‑machine learning framework
abstract: In this study, the dynamic behavior of an axially moving functionally graded (FG) plate composed of perovskite and piezoelectric ceramic constituents is examined. The structure is subjected to coupled light illumination, electric field, and yawed supersonic flow. A unified multiphysics-data-driven framework is developed to examine the effects of key parameters, including aspect ratio, boundary conditions, in-plane forces, and variable-stiffness elastic foundations. Stability analysis is carried out to determine divergence and flutter boundaries using the generalized differential quadrature method (GDQM) combined with an eigenvalue solution. In addition, two machine learning models, namely ε-support vector regression (ε-SVR) and artificial neural networks (ANN), are employed as efficient surrogate predictors. Their performance is assessed using parity plots, Bland-Altman analysis, error histograms, and Taylor diagrams. The results reveal that light-induced photostriction and thermal effects significantly reduce aeroelastic stability margins, while increasing the electric field lowers the critical axial speed due to electrostrictive and piezoelectric coupling. Decreasing the material gradient index is shown to mitigate these destabilizing effects. Among the models, the medium-sized ANN and cubic-SVR achieve the highest prediction accuracy, whereas linear-SVR exhibits underfitting behavior. The proposed framework provides an accurate and computationally efficient tool for analyzing vibration and aeroelastic instability of idealized smart FG plates under coupled multiphysics loading conditions and may offer useful insights for the preliminary assessment of advanced aerospace structures.

title: Analysis of formation flight aerodynamics using vortex lattice method and convolutional neural networks
abstract: Significant fuel savings can be obtained in formation flight by taking advantage of wake vortices if the relative position of aircraft can be effectively optimized. In this paper, formation flight of a leader and a follower unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) is investigated. The location of the follower UAV is varied relative to the leader while flying at various angles of attack, with the wing sweep angle varied between positive and negative values corresponding to forward-swept and swept-back configurations. An in-house code is developed based on the Vortex Lattice Method (VLM) that incorporates such variations in formation flight and is used in conjunction with machine learning to calculate the resulting aerodynamic coefficients of forces and moments. For doing so, the relative spacing and angles are encoded into a structured input representation and the calculated coefficients by the VLM are used to train a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) model. Results show that the maximum drag reduction increases as the angle of attack and sweep angle are increased. For negative sweep angles, however, drag tends to increase due to downwash at certain locations behind the leader UAV, resulting in no drag reduction possibility at those locations. Among all sweep angles studied, the forward-swept configuration is observed to cause pronounced differences in lift and rolling moment coefficients. Similarly, the swept-back configuration with the highest sweep angle gives the largest difference in pitching moment. Comparison of the results from the trained CNN model with those from the VLM code shows that the CNN is capable of providing a quick and satisfactory assessment of the aerodynamic performance of formation flights compared to the VLM and that it can successfully predict the location of the sweet spot for different flight configurations.

title: An adaptive physics-informed graph neural network-based method for aero-engine gas path estimation
abstract: Precise estimation of gas path parameters is essential for effective aero-engine health management, despite the inherent complexity of aero-engine internal structures. A reliable estimation model can be characterized as a virtual sensor. The discrepancy between measured data and the estimates from a reliable model reflects the health status of an aero-engine. This study develops an Adaptive Physics-Informed Graph Neural Network Model, termed API-GNN. The model comprises a directed graph neural network, a temporal feature extraction module, independent processing channels, and a composite loss function. The directed graph neural network improves the physical consistency of the API-GNN through the explicit introduction of physics-based directional constraints. The temporal feature extraction module characterizes multi-scale response delay properties through a parallel heterogeneous network and an explicit memory unit. Independent processing channels enhance the estimation accuracy of the API-GNN by separately addressing distinct flight conditions. The composite loss function improves estimation accuracy while incorporating engineering-informed physical constraints. Furthermore, a local parameter updating strategy enhances the adaptability of the API-GNN, achieving a balance between update efficiency and generalization capability. The API-GNN exhibits superior predictive performance to conventional methods over the aero-engine life cycle, as verified by real flight data.

title: Recent application progress of graph neural networks in computational fluid dynamics
abstract: Traditional computational fluid dynamics (CFD) suffers from inherent numerical bottlenecks in complex geometric adaptation, unstructured mesh calculation and high-cost iterative solving, failing to balance simulation accuracy and computational efficiency for complex engineering flow problems. With the rapid development of artificial intelligence, deep learning has become a promising surrogate modelling paradigm for intelligent CFD, yet conventional grid-based methods such as convolutional neural networks (CNNs) are limited in representing unstructured data and multi-scale physical flow interactions. Graph neural networks (GNNs) exhibit unique structural advantages, as CFD discretization systems including meshes, particles and flux adjacency can be naturally mapped to graph topological structures and message-passing mechanisms. This review systematically summarizes the state-of-the-art GNN applications in CFD from four core optimization dimensions: graph construction, message passing, physical constraint embedding and hybrid numerical solving. The adaptive characteristics of GNNs in diverse flow scenarios, including turbulence, compressible flow, fluid-structure interaction and sparse flow field reconstruction, are further clarified. Current GNN-CFD techniques still face challenges in unified benchmark standards, complex flow generalization capability, computational overhead and physical interpretability for trustworthy engineering applications. Future research will focus on the deep integration of physics-aware graph learning and traditional numerical methods to develop scalable, stable and interpretable intelligent CFD solving systems.

title: Hybrid Physics-Informed Neural Network with Integrated Physical Constraints for Propeller Noise Prediction
abstract: With the widespread application of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) in various fields, propeller noise has become a key constraint limiting their urban operations, while traditional noise prediction methods suffer from inherent flaws—empirical models prioritize efficiency over accuracy, and data-driven approaches lack physical interpretability and rely heavily on large datasets. To address these issues, this study proposes a Hybrid Physics-Informed Neural Network (HybridPINN) for propeller noise prediction. The core idea is to embed FW-H-based acoustic scaling laws in a fixed physics branch and combine them with a trainable residual corrector, thereby coupling deep learning with interpretable physical structure. To mitigate data scarcity, a data augmentation method is adopted to enhance dataset representativeness. The model features a dual-branch fusion architecture: the physics branch generates physically compliant total-noise predictions, while the data-driven branch learns residuals to compensate for systematic errors of the physical surrogate. Experimental validation shows that the framework outperforms traditional machine learning models, accurately capturing noise variation trends under the coupling of operational and geometric factors while avoiding unphysical predictions. This work provides a technical solution integrating prediction accuracy and physical interpretability, supporting the design of low-noise UAV propellers and promoting urban UAV applications.

title: Impact-induced reaction evolution in solid rocket motors: SPH simulation and physics-informed prediction
abstract: High-speed fragment impact can induce shock-driven ignition and violent reactions in solid rocket motors (SRMs), posing severe safety risks. However, the coupled effects of fragment velocity and structural size on reaction evolution remain unclear, and efficient predictive approaches are lacking. In this study, a smoothed particle hydrodynamics (SPH) framework is developed to simulate the coupled mechanical–thermal–chemical response of SRMs under fragment impact, and is validated against light-gas gun experiments. A pressure-based criterion is proposed to distinguish shock propagation regimes and identify the onset of enhanced shock-reaction coupling. Results show that for the propellant studied in the present work a critical velocity range of 1600–1800 m s⁻¹ marks the transition from attenuating to self-amplifying shock propagation. Increasing velocity significantly enhances reaction intensity, while structural size exhibits a clear scale effect, with smaller motors promoting rapid initiation and larger motors favoring extensive reaction growth and higher reacting mass. A physics-informed Kolmogorov–Arnold network (PI-KAN) is further developed for rapid prediction of global reaction behavior, achieving high accuracy (R² = 0.96). The results provide a quantitative framework for understanding and predicting impact-induced reactions in SRMs.

title: Physics informed machine learning based predictive control for intelligent operation of edge datacenters
abstract: Edge data centers (EDCs) are critical for supporting latency-sensitive applications; however, their high energy consumption, especially in cooling systems, presents significant sustainability challenges that are further compounded by recent advancements in Artificial Intelligence (AI). In recent years, integrating AI with Model Predictive Control (MPC) has shown promise in reducing cooling energy consumption while maintaining operational safety, but most AI models remain impractical for real-world deployment. This limitation arises from their inherent black-box nature and heavy dependence on the quantity and quality of training data, which hampers their ability to handle unseen conditions effectively. To address these challenges, we propose a physics-informed machine learning-based MPC (PIML-MPC) framework that integrates physical principles into neural networks to improve prediction accuracy. By embedding established physical knowledge, our approach enhances model generalization and reduces its dependence on extensive training data. We validated the framework using a simulation model derived from real data center measurements. Experimental results show that the PIML-MPC strategy reduces energy consumption by 12.6 % compared to a baseline, without compromising thermal regulation. Under unseen high heat load conditions, the framework further reduces energy consumption by 9.1 % while maintaining thermal performance, demonstrating robust generalization. Moreover, across ten randomized trials, PIML-MPC consistently outperforms three advanced time-series and machine-learning-based MPC schemes—achieving superior energy efficiency, tighter thermal control, and reduced sensitivity to stochastic variations. This work paves the way for the practical adoption of AI-driven MPC in data center cooling by substantially improving the generalization performance of AI controllers.

title: A novel probabilistic wind power forecasting framework integrating similar curve matching mechanism and an enhanced conditional diffusion model
abstract: Achieving carbon neutrality is a global priority, with wind power playing a key role in the sustainable energy transition. However, its inherent uncertainty poses challenges to power grid stability. To address this, we propose a novel probabilistic wind power forecasting framework that integrates a Similar Curve Matching Mechanism (SCMM) with an enhanced conditional diffusion model to improve uncertainty quantification. We introduce a Conditional-Denoising Joint Network (CDJN) that dynamically processes condition information, enhancing model expressiveness compared to static encoding. To account for the heterogeneity of wind power generation, SCMM leverages K-Medoids clustering and Fast-Dynamic Time Warping (Fast-DTW) to generate customized training sets, enabling the model to capture diverse wind power patterns with greater accuracy. The trained conditional diffusion model generates a large set of wind power scenarios, from which a Gated Recurrent Unit-based Autoencoder (GRUA) and Kernel Density Estimation (KDE) are applied to produce reliable probabilistic forecasts with time dependencies. This novel approach effectively enhances forecasting precision and adaptability. Case studies using real wind farm data from Ordos, Inner Mongolia, China, demonstrate that the proposed framework significantly outperforms state-of-the-art models across multiple evaluation metrics. Notably, the ablation study indicates that removing key components caused a 469.21 % increase in average loss, highlighting the critical role of each module. The results highlight its improved ability to measure wind power uncertainty and improve forecasting accuracy, hence being a promising solution to incorporate wind power into power systems more reliably.

title: Battery health prediction under data scarcity: A cross-domain physics-informed 5-shot framework with GRU-Transformer
abstract: Battery health prediction faces multi-factor challenges. Significant differences exist in degradation patterns across material systems and usage scenarios. Traditional models relying on homogeneous data struggle with complex operating conditions. This study innovatively proposes a 5-shot meta-learning framework to accurately predict battery health under data scarcity. Experiments employ dual-threshold truncation for multi-source data processing, eliminating sensor noise interference. By analyzing capacity decay dynamics, we design a physics-informed loss function that embeds electrochemical mechanisms into a gated recurrent unit-Transformer hybrid architecture. Combined with cross-domain transfer strategies, the model achieves high-precision, robust predictions through physical law constraints and meta-learning fast adaptation. The constructed multi-physics synergistic model integrates diffusion-reaction-bias dynamics, while dynamic masking enhances small-sample adaptability. 349,443 cross-material query tests demonstrate model MAPE as low as 0.45 % with R2 reaching 0.9634, validating the effectiveness of physical constraints and meta-transfer mechanisms.
