title: A cross-modal deep learning framework based on dual-branch enhanced CNN and mamba for intra-day solar irradiance forecasting
abstract: Accurate solar irradiance forecasting is essential for improving the economics and stability of building energy systems. Although existing multimodal deep learning methods have improved forecasting accuracy by integrating meteorological data with satellite cloud images, they still suffer from insufficient cloud feature extraction, inadequate modeling of temporal dependencies, and limited capability of uncertainty quantification under complex weather conditions. To address these issues, this study proposed an end-to-end multimodal deep learning framework for intra-day solar irradiance forecasting by integrating meteorological data with satellite cloud images. Specifically, Mamba blocks were employed to efficiently capture complex temporal dependencies in meteorological sequences, while a global-local dual-branch image encoder based on frequency-mixed and feature-enhanced convolutional neural networks (CNNs) was developed to extract multi-scale cloud features. Furthermore, a cross-modal interaction mechanism and an encoder-decoder-based future modeling strategy were introduced to enable deep multimodal fusion. Dual-output heads are further employed to jointly generate point forecasts and prediction intervals. Experimental results show that the proposed method consistently outperforms recent advanced multimodal benchmarks across different forecasting horizons and weather conditions, demonstrating strong robustness and generalization capability. In particular, the proposed model achieves relative reductions of 16.39%–21.18% in MAPE and 10.11%–14.31% in nRMSE in point forecasting, while achieving a favorable balance between reliability and sharpness in interval forecasting. Ablation studies and cross-site experiments further verify the effectiveness, robustness, and applicability of the proposed model. This work provides an effective and robust solution for high-accuracy intra-day solar irradiance forecasting.

title: Hierarchical symbolic regression for multi-component wind-turbine wake modeling under varying turbulence
abstract: The reliable prediction of wind turbine wakes under varying environmental conditions remains a major challenge for wind farm design and operation. In this study, we employ a hierarchical symbolic regression approach to derive interpretable mathematical expressions for wake velocity deficits, providing a full three-component representation of streamwise, vertical, and spanwise flow behavior—a capability largely absent from conventional analytical models. Incoming turbulence intensity is explicitly incorporated, enabling the models to adapt across diverse atmospheric conditions. To address discontinuities arising in the hierarchical decomposition, a weighted symbolic regression strategy is introduced that enhances robustness and solution stability. The resulting expressions are concise and interpretable, and their hierarchical combination for wake velocity prediction is extensively validated against an expansive multi-source dataset of 166 independent profiles. Spanning extreme turbulence scenarios (up to 21%), this validation confirms the model’s robust generalizability. Furthermore, our approach demonstrates significantly improved predictive accuracy for streamwise velocity, particularly in the near-wake region where conventional assumptions break down, while offering a complete solution for the full three-dimensional flow field. These results highlight symbolic regression as a systematic pathway for deriving computationally efficient, equation-based wake models. Consequently, the proposed framework can be seamlessly integrated into wind farm layout optimization, directly enhancing annual energy production estimates and reducing the levelized cost of energy.

title: ResistNet: Quantifying solar energy reduction during hurricanes with deep learning
abstract: Solar energy is central to the clean energy transition, accounting for a large share of newly installed renewable capacity in recent years. Extreme weather events, particularly hurricanes with extensive cloud systems, can cause substantial reductions in solar photovoltaic generation. Traditional statistical approaches and physics-based simulations struggle to forecast these hurricane-induced reductions both efficiently and accurately. To address this gap, we introduce ResistNet, a machine learning framework based on high-resolution solar irradiance data and comprehensive storm characteristics across the Atlantic basin over two decades. Built on an encoder-decoder transformer architecture with multi-head self-attention and cross-attention mechanisms, ResistNet integrates time-evolving hurricane dynamics with station-specific contextual features to predict solar energy reduction at fine spatial and temporal scales. Our experiments using an event-based five-fold cross-validation scheme demonstrate improved predictive accuracy over traditional statistical and machine learning baselines. ResistNet achieves the lowest overall MSE and MAE among the compared models and consistently improves prediction accuracy across cross-validation folds, highlighting its robustness and generalizability. ResistNet provides an efficient tool for enhancing solar energy forecasting, planning, and resilient grid operations under intensifying climate extremes.

title: Physics-informed reinforcement learning for energy-efficient minute-scale control of split-type air-conditioning systems: Experimental validation on real hardware
abstract: This study presents the full online deployment of reinforcement learning on a real commercial split-type air-conditioning system. The experimental campaign consists of 58 real-hardware runs with approximately 207 h of cumulative interaction, enabling analysis of long-horizon online learning behavior under actual hardware constraints. Motivated by practical difficulties observed during deployment, a physics-informed reinforcement learning framework is developed. Hardware experiments reveal several failure modes, including unsafe brute-force cooling, compressor-dominated local convergence, insufficient actuator coordination, and holding-stage oscillations. To address these issues, the proposed framework integrates physics-informed components and value-learning components. The physics-informed design incorporates three layers: a structural layer for hierarchical compressor–EEV control, a constraint layer enforcing manufacturer-informed feasible operating regions, and a signal layer introducing delayed-response-aware state representations and phase-dependent rewards. The value-learning component is based on D3QN and incorporates lightweight stabilization techniques to support reliable online learning under delayed and limited feedback. Through these interventions, the controller evolves toward stable, coordinated, and anticipatory operation while maintaining a compact Q-network with two 32-neuron hidden layers suitable for embedded implementation. In a 140-min matched-comfort evaluation, the RL controller reaches the ±0.5 °C comfort band faster than the factory-calibrated PID baseline (33 min vs. 40 min) and maintains comparable regulation quality thereafter. It achieves a 19.0% reduction in total energy consumption across pull-down and holding phases. The learned policy operates with coordinated low-frequency compressor behavior, increased valve utilization, reduced condenser-side thermal stress, and preserved indoor-side heat exchange. Supporting experiments across different laboratories, setpoints, and load conditions further demonstrate robustness and adaptability. These results provide a deployable pathway for applying physics-informed reinforcement learning to compact, fast-response, and computationally constrained energy systems.

title: How does AI family drive the industrial chain upgrading of solar cells?
abstract: AI families, including machine learning, deep learning, and large language models, significantly drive solar cell (SC) industry upgrades. However, current research exhibits disciplinary fragmentation, typically focusing on single AI models within specific technologies like Silicon (SSC), Dye-sensitized (DSC), and Perovskite (PSC) cells. This creates a critical gap: the lack of comprehensive macro level framework explaining how the AI family propels innovation across distinct technological pathways. Therefore, our research constructs a universal innovation framework designed for analyzing the driving logic of the AI family on the development of SSC, DSC, and PSC. The framework leverages a large-scale dataset of patent documents and applies advanced Natural Language Processing techniques, including Named Entity Recognition and BERT-based models, to quantify AI's impact. The analysis is further synthesized through visualizations such as spherical networks and canopy graphs. Our research reveals that AI integration in the solar industry is not an arbitrary process but follows a structured trajectory governed by three core principles. First, a technology's maturity dictates the complexity of AI integration, with more mature technologies like SSC exhibiting more intricate AI applications. Second, AI tools are selected with high specificity to address the unique technical challenges of each cell type. Third, AI adoption follows a predictable sequence, progressing from foundational Machine Learning, to advanced Deep Learning, and finally toward cutting-edge Large Language Models. Significantly, the proposed framework successfully decodes predictable patterns in AI driven solar innovation, establishing a theoretical foundation for accelerating technological breakthroughs across the entire SC industrial chain. The three distinct AI and SC phenomena enable industry practitioners to optimize resource allocation, thereby enhancing the overall efficiency of future energy transitions.

abstract:
Lithium-ion batteries for second-life utilization used in shared electric bikes face elevated safety risks due to the lack of historical operating conditions, capacity degradation, and increased internal resistance. To enable timely and accurate diagnosis under sparse cloud conditions, this article proposes a two-stage diagnostic framework for multi-fault identification in battery packs. To achieve fault cells classification, six strong correlation features with battery faults from the voltage difference and energy factor are employed to establish the TabNet deep learning network model. Finally, the TabNet model is validated using 30 s sparse cloud-based charging data from shared electric bikes. The fault detection rate and fault classification accuracy of this method are 99.43% and 99.13%, respectively, effectively enabling multi-fault diagnosis of lithium-ion battery packs using sparse cloud-based charging data.

title: Meta-cognitive AutoEvo control for residential HVAC: A cascaded physics-informed HDeePC-MPC framework with bounded self-reconfiguration
abstract: To address weak mechanistic priors, time-varying dynamics, and control-oriented model mismatch in residential Heating, Ventilation, and Air Conditioning (HVAC) systems, this paper proposes a cascaded physics-informed data-driven predictive control framework for residential inverter split-type air conditioners. The architecture uses a slow outer-loop Hankel Data-Enabled Predictive Control (HDeePC) layer for indoor-temperature regulation and a fast inner-loop Model Predictive Control (MPC) layer for coil-temperature tracking. Runtime physical consistency is introduced through dual-layer physics-informed constraints: PIC-Hard screens physically inconsistent inner-loop N4SID models, while PIC-Soft regularizes outer-loop HDeePC predictions toward a first-law-based temperature trajectory. For bounded online adaptation, an Autonomous Evolution (AutoEvo) self-reconfiguration module combines KPI-based self-evaluation, archive retrieval, LLM-assisted structured candidate generation, and parameter-side admissibility projection, so that hyperparameter-level recovery remains inside the constrained predictive-control stack. Closed-loop chamber experiments on a residential inverter split-type air conditioner show that the proposed framework reduces indoor-temperature IAE and same-meter energy consumption by 34.9% and 28.6%, respectively, relative to an industrial multi-loop PID baseline over the evaluated variable-load intervals. In the tested sequential out-of-distribution switch validation, enabling PIC helps the controller escape low-frequency compressor saturation and reduces window-normalized tracking-error intensity by approximately 65% in both direct and equal-window bootstrap estimates. Under deliberate admissible parameter degradation, AutoEvo reduces MAE from 0.51 to 0.33⁢∘⁢C and mean electrical power from 635.1 to 515.6 W. Together, the chamber results support the combination of cascaded HDeePC-MPC, runtime physical consistency, and bounded parameter-side self-reconfiguration for single-zone residential HVAC control.

title: A physics-guided neural network with battery constraint mechanism for state-of-energy estimation of lithium-ion batteries
abstract: Numerous studies have investigated the application of neural network models for state-of-energy (SOE) estimation. However, purely data-driven approaches fail to capture the underlying battery operation mechanism during modeling; hence the model parameters can only be optimized through a trial-and-error process, which limits the model’s performance. This paper investigates a physics-guided neural network with a battery constraint mechanism for SOE estimation of lithium-ion batteries (LIBs). A physics-guided neural network incorporating the power integration method (PIM) is designed for SOE estimation, and an incremental PIM-based constraint is constructed using the reference SOE trajectory available during training. By analyzing the principles of model parameter optimization, an adaptive weight adjustment method is proposed for the PIM-based incremental constraint. During the model inference stage, a PIM-based monitoring mechanism is employed in the sliding-window, and a consistency score is defined to mitigate prediction drift during SOE estimation, thereby improving the reliability of online predictions from the pre-trained model. The proposed method is validated under various cycle profiles, including tests with 18650-type LIBs, electric vehicle power batteries, and real-world BEV data. The ablation studies further demonstrate its effectiveness.

title: Physics-informed machine learning-based adaptive predictive control for energy-efficient hybrid-cooled data centers management
abstract: Data centers (DCs) support digital services but consume substantial cooling energy, a challenge intensified by the rapid growth of AI workloads. Although previous studies have shown that integrating physics-informed machine learning (PIML) with model predictive control (MPC) can improve cooling performance, most existing approaches rely on static models trained on limited datasets and do not examine whether these advantages persist under long-term, data-rich operation with periodic updating. To address this gap, this study proposes a PIML-based adaptive MPC (PIML-AMPC) framework for the intelligent and energy-efficient operation of hybrid-cooled DCs. The framework combines physics-informed predictive modeling with periodic fine-tuning to adapt to evolving system dynamics, workloads, and environmental conditions. A simulation model, developed using real operational data from the STDCT testbed, is used to evaluate the proposed strategy over a ten-month period. The results show that PIML-AMPC eliminates thermal violations and reduces total cooling-energy consumption by 23.5% relative to a baseline fixed-setpoint controller. Compared with three representative model-based MPC methods, PIML-AMPC consistently achieves additional energy savings, improved temperature regulation, and stronger robustness to random factors. These advantages are most evident during data-limited early deployment, when historical DC data are typically collected under traditional control strategies and thus lack sufficient diversity. PIML-AMPC also generalizes well across three climatic regions, achieving 23.5%–26.5% cooling-energy savings. Overall, this work advances the practical deployment of physics-informed, AI-enhanced MPC for sustainable and thermally reliable DC cooling.

title: Risk-aware resistance enhancement for integrated heat and power supply driven by physics-informed meteorological data
abstract: Cold extremes bring significant uncertainties to the energy system. Their strong spatiotemporal coupling introduces growing challenges to the adequacy and flexibility of the power and heating supply, complicating risk identification and mitigation. Therefore, this paper presents a framework for spatiotemporal risk assessment and resistance enhancement under cold extremes. It captures cold-air propagation using a trajectory-informed method and quantifies the inadequacy of the heating supply through multiple risk indicators. Based on this, a risk-aware scheduling strategy is developed to improve the coordination of power and heating supply and enhance system resistance during cold extremes. Empirical studies on the biomass-based combined heat and power supply in Sweden demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach in reducing heating supply inadequacy and external energy dependence.

title: Adaptive look-ahead economic dispatch with reinforcement learning for virtual power plant considering uncertainty
abstract: Virtual power plant (VPP) aggregates numerous distributed resources to respond to power grid demands. To achieve long-term and stable operation, look-ahead economic dispatch (LAED) of VPPs is a key technology. However, traditional methods typically assume that the Look-ahead horizon is set according to a fixed strategy, while neglecting the variability of risk preferences for balance between robustness and economic efficiency in a dynamic environment. To address these issues, this paper proposes an adaptive LAED method with reinforcement learning framework considering uncertainty. This approach constructs the dispatch model with day-in correction process based on distributionally robust optimization. The look-ahead horizon and adjustable robustness parameters are abstracted as the decision variables under the reinforcement learning framework. To efficiently obtain optimal values for the above parameters, a transformer-PPO optimization algorithm is presented. Based on simulation data analysis, the proposed method can precisely balance the robustness and economic efficiency Compared to other mainstream methods, the proposed method not only achieves higher profits (Up to 32.76%) but also enhances better power grid demands responsiveness (Up to 14.79%).

title: Dynamic soiling-state inversion and power prediction for photovoltaic modules via gradient-coupled physics-informed neural networks
abstract: Dust accumulation on photovoltaic (PV) module surfaces is a key factor leading to reduced power generation efficiency, and its dynamic evolution is jointly influenced by meteorological conditions and cleaning events. Addressing the limitations of existing methods, which struggle to achieve high-resolution continuous state inversion and often lack physical consistency in prediction models, this paper proposes a gradient-coupled Ordinary Differential Equations (ODEs)-Physics-Informed Neural Network (PINN) prediction framework that deeply integrates physical mechanisms with data-driven approaches. Firstly, a robust proxy label for the PV module soiling state is constructed based on the physical characteristics of the PV cell short-circuit current, and a learnable dynamic model centered on ODEs is established to enable differentiable modeling of both deposition and cleaning processes. Secondly, a PINN-constrained power prediction model is designed, incorporating the photovoltaic conversion physical equations as regularization terms. Furthermore, a gradient coupling mechanism is introduced, facilitating end-to-end optimization of the soiling-state inversion network through the power prediction loss via differentiable computational graphs. Based on real-world operational data collected and processed in accordance with the IEA PVPS Task 13, the experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves an RMSE of 0.0217 for point-wise soiling-state inversion, with a coefficient of determination R2 of 0.977. In terms of power prediction, the RMSE is reduced by approximately 42.9% compared to the best-performing purely data-driven baseline model. Furthermore, the framework shows stable prediction behavior and physical consistency under the bad weather conditions included in the test set.

title: State of energy estimation of lithium-ion batteries based on Bayesian-optimized bidirectional temporal convolutional neural network with ECM-based feature extraction and bidirectional filtering
abstract: Accurate estimation of the state of energy (SOE) in lithium-ion batteries is crucial for assessing the remaining driving range of electric vehicles (EVs). However, complex operating conditions make high-precision SOE estimation challenging. This paper develops a physics-guided cascaded deep learning framework for high-precision SOE estimation, which systematically addresses key modeling challenges, namely nonlinear temporal modeling, limited physical interpretability, and susceptibility to measurement disturbances. Specifically, an optimized bidirectional temporal convolutional network (BiTCN) is employed as the core estimator to capture the complex nonlinear temporal dynamics of SOE. To guide temporal representation learning with physically meaningful information, equivalent circuit model (ECM) characteristic parameters identified using the time-varying discount factor recursive least squares (TDFRLS) algorithm are integrated with externally measurable signals to construct physics-informed input features. Furthermore, a bidirectional filtering strategy is incorporated into the framework to improve robustness against measurement disturbances and reduce estimation fluctuations under dynamic operating conditions. Experimental results demonstrate that, under cross-operating-condition and cross-battery-type scenarios, the maximum absolute estimation errors of the proposed framework are 0.0200 and 0.0187, effectively verifying the estimation accuracy and generalization capability.

title: PVDINO: Extracting photovoltaic panels from high-resolution remote sensing imagery via vision foundation model and dual-stream edge mining
abstract: Accurate extraction of large-scale photovoltaic (PV) facilities from high-resolution satellite and Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) imagery is crucial for achieving global carbon neutrality. However, existing methods struggle to balance deep semantic representation with fine-grained edge localization amidst multi-scale morphological variations and complex background interferences. To overcome this limitation, this paper pioneers the introduction of the self-supervised vision foundation model (DINOv3) into remote sensing PV extraction by proposing PVDINO, a novel end-to-end framework. First, a DINOv3 Semantic Adaptation Encoder effectively adapts multi-level features to enhance deep global semantic representation. Second, an Edge Feature Mining Encoder introduces frequency-domain priors and flow field estimation for the fine-grained mining of shallow and deep features, respectively. Finally, a Cross-Guided Fusion Decoder synergizes these global semantic and edge-enhanced features for highly accurate extraction. Extensive experiments on the AIR-PV, PVP, and H-RPVS datasets demonstrate PVDINO’s superiority. Notably, it yields an F1-score of 96.78% and an Intersection over Union (IoU) of 93.88% on the PVP dataset, outperforming state-of-the-art methods by up to 1.61% in IoU. Furthermore, PVDINO exhibits exceptional robustness in cross-scene generalization and large-scale mapping, providing a reliable automated monitoring solution for macro-energy infrastructure. The source code will be available at: https://github.com/whuzzzz/PVDINO.

title: A dual-diffusion model for hydrogel-based photovoltaic cooling: Climatic adaptability and national application potential
abstract: Hydrogel-based evaporative cooling offers a promising strategy for photovoltaic (PV) thermal management, yet a comprehensive model integrating both internal and external evaporation remains lacking. Additionally, the long-term hygroscopic stability and water replenishment sustainability of hydrogels under diverse climatic conditions also remain largely unexplored. In this work, we develop a dual-diffusion model (DDM) that simultaneously captures evaporation at the hydrogel micropores and the external air/gel interface. Experimental validation using fabricated PV/HG modules showed a mean relative error of 2.39% for PV surface temperature, and achieves a maximum temperature reduction of 23.5 °C and an average power enhancement of 17.8%. Micropore evaporation and external interface evaporation respectively contribute 24% and 76% of the total cooling power, indicating that neither mechanism should be overlooked. Parametric studies reveal that a salt concentration of 30 wt% optimally balances cooling performance with moisture replenishment. Long-term testing under Hong Kong summer conditions demonstrated an average temperature reduction of 2.28 °C and stable water content (∼95%). Nationwide simulations across 34 provinces and nine representative cities reveal a clear trade-off where arid northern regions achieve larger temperature drops (up to 3.93 °C) and higher power gains (2.0–2.3%) but require frequent hydrogel replacements (up to 24 times per year), whereas humid southern regions offer lower gains (1.3–1.7%) with minimal maintenance. An economic analysis indicates that the raw material cost of the hydrogel cooling layer is approximately 10% of the PV panel cost. Overall, this work provides a unified framework for hydrogel-based thermal management and practical guidance for diverse climates.

title: A radiative-state guided debiasing transformer for patch-wise day-ahead photovoltaic power forecasting
abstract: Accurate day-ahead photovoltaic (PV) power forecasting is essential for the reliable operation of renewable-dominated power systems, but remains challenging due to strong radiative variability and seasonal dependency. Existing methods mainly rely on data-driven correlation learning, while physics-informed approaches typically introduce physical knowledge through input features, normalization, or loss constraints, leaving attention-level interaction modeling and representation bias insufficiently addressed. To address these limitations, this study proposes a Radiative-State Guided Debiasing Transformer (RSGDT) for patch-wise day-ahead PV forecasting. RSGDT consists of two key components: Radiative-State Guided Attention (RSGA) and Seasonal Debiasing Regularization (SDR). Specifically, RSGA incorporates radiative-state information derived from solar geometry and atmospheric transmittance into the attention mechanism through pairwise radiative-state distance-aware logit modulation, thereby enabling radiative-state guided token-level interactions. SDR further mitigates seasonal shortcut dependence in latent embeddings at the representation level, improving robustness under varying radiative conditions. Experiments demonstrate that RSGDT consistently achieves lower forecasting errors than statistical, deep learning, and physics-informed baselines. A simplified single-bus operational proxy analysis using reserve, balancing-cost, and curtailment indicators further suggests that improved forecasting accuracy may reduce operational burden under the simplified assumptions, while serving only as a relative and illustrative evaluation rather than a full system-level dispatch study.

title: Frequency-coordinated conditional diffusion model for extreme-value-aware wind power forecasting
abstract: Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Models (DDPMs) have shown distinct advantages in probabilistic wind power forecasting owing to their progressive denoising mechanism. However, existing DDPM-based approaches mainly focus on capturing the global statistical properties of wind power and modeling its temporal dynamics, while showing clear limitations in characterizing extreme values defined by the Peaks Over Threshold (POT). To address this problem, this paper proposes a novel forecasting method that combines temporal information with rich frequency-domain features, taking into account the differences in noise attenuation rates across different frequency components. First, a frequency separation mechanism based on spectral energy density is used to automatically separate low-frequency components encoding global structures from high-frequency components capturing fine-grained fluctuations. Second, an adaptive high-frequency augmentation strategy is designed to apply distinct coefficients based on the attenuation characteristics of each frequency component, thereby preventing premature decay of extreme values. Third, a dual-branch denoising network is proposed that jointly leverages trend extraction in the temporal domain and spectral information in the frequency domain. Finally, the standard DDPM is extended with POT conditioning, and the generalized Pareto distribution is incorporated into the loss function to ensure fidelity to both the POT and overall data distributions. Experimental results on two datasets confirm the effectiveness of the proposed method, underscoring its potential to advance diffusion model-based wind power forecasting, particularly in the accurate modeling of extreme events.

title: A physics-informed transformer-KAN network for privacy-enhanced multi-prosumer energy trading in distribution systems
abstract: Existing multi-prosumer energy trading methods still face privacy leakage risks, limited deployability, and insufficient adaptability. This paper first establishes a proof framework for the existence and uniqueness of the multi-prosumer equilibrium price under intertemporal storage constraints. This analysis provides a theoretical foundation for the subsequent market-clearing algorithm. A physics-informed multi-prosumer trading method is then proposed. In this method, each participant interacts with the platform through a local surrogate model rather than uploading raw data. The trading platform obtains the 24-period equilibrium clearing price sequence through response sampling, feature extraction, state aggregation, and price mapping. Market supply-demand imbalance is embedded into the loss function as physical information, thereby enabling unsupervised training. Case studies show that the proposed method enhances participants' privacy while achieving robust convergence, accurate market clearing, and strong adaptability and scalability. Under normal operating conditions, the proposed method reduces the maximum market imbalance by more than 90% compared with the conventional PINN method. Under renewable generation fault scenarios, it reduces the maximum imbalance by about 94% compared with multi-agent reinforcement learning. The proposed framework reduces online communication and computation, demonstrating its potential for practical distribution-level multi-prosumer trading.

title: PMGT-Net: A physics-informed multi-scale graph transformer framework for explainable national energy dependency forecasting
abstract: Accurate forecasting of national energy dependency is critically important for sustainable energy planning, energy security, and strategic policy development. However, national energy systems exhibit highly complex temporal dynamics, interdependent energy relationships, and nonlinear consumption–import interactions, making reliable forecasting a challenging task. Existing forecasting approaches generally focus on temporal modeling while insufficiently capturing dynamic relational dependencies among multiple energy components. To address these limitations, this study proposes a Physics-Informed Multi-Scale Graph Transformer Network (PMGT-Net) framework for national energy dependency forecasting using monthly EMRA/EPDK energy data. The proposed framework integrates multi-scale temporal learning, dynamic graph construction, Graph Transformer-based relational modeling, and physics-informed optimization within a unified forecasting architecture. Unlike existing energy forecasting approaches that primarily emphasize temporal modeling or address graph learning, physics-informed optimization, and explainability as separate components, PMGT-Net jointly integrates these complementary mechanisms within a unified end-to-end framework specifically designed for national energy dependency forecasting. In addition, explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) mechanisms are incorporated to improve interpretability and analyze the contribution of individual energy variables to forecasting decisions. The framework models complex interactions among electricity, natural gas, petroleum, and LPG production–consumption–import variables while simultaneously learning long-term temporal dependencies and energy-balance constraints. Extensive experiments were conducted using comparative deep learning and Transformer-based baseline models, including LSTM, GRU, Bi-LSTM, Transformer, Informer, Autoformer, FEDformer, PatchTST, iTransformer and ST-GNN architectures. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed PMGT-Net framework achieves superior forecasting performance with lower RMSE, MAE, and MAPE values compared with all comparative models. Ablation analyses confirm the effectiveness of each architectural component, while robustness analyses demonstrate stable forecasting capability under noisy, missing-value, and seasonal-shift scenarios. Furthermore, statistical significance tests verify that the observed performance improvements are statistically meaningful. Explainability analyses reveal that natural gas imports, petroleum-related indicators, and electricity consumption are among the most influential variables affecting national energy dependency forecasting. Overall, the proposed PMGT-Net framework provides an effective, interpretable, and physically informed forecasting solution for national energy dependency analysis. The framework can support energy policy development, strategic energy planning, sustainable resource management, and decision-support systems for future smart energy infrastructures.

title: Multi-scale physics-informed neural network-based temperature modeling and prediction for real vehicle battery systems
abstract: With the widespread adoption of fast charging and high-power operation in electric vehicles (EVs), battery temperature has become a critical safety variable closely linked to thermal runaway, highlighting the need for accurate temperature prediction in real vehicles. Therefore, this study proposes a physics-informed neural network (PINN) framework for accurate and robust temperature prediction of battery systems under real vehicle conditions. The study validates the capability of PINNs for reconstructing the two-dimensional (2D) temperature field estimation of 18,650 cells by embedding heat conduction equations and identifying key thermal parameters. On this basis, a system-level PINN constrained by a lumped thermal energy balance is developed for real vehicle battery temperature prediction, where hierarchical clustering is employed to construct proxy temperatures from sparse and heterogeneous sensors. The proposed framework is systematically evaluated through multi-condition accuracy validation, comparison with machine and deep learning baselines, and cross-vehicle transfer tests using data from multiple real EVs. Results show that the PINN accurately reconstructs cell-level 2D temperature fields with errors within 2 K, while achieving stable system-level temperature prediction under real-vehicle conditions, with R2 consistently above 0.99 across different time periods and thermal regions. Compared with baseline models, the PINN maintains superior robustness during rapid temperature fluctuations and demonstrates strong generalization, with cross-vehicle maximum prediction errors controlled within [0.31, 1.49] °C. This work explores the application of PINNs for real vehicle battery system temperature prediction, providing a physically consistent and scalable solution for thermal safety monitoring in practical battery management systems.

title: AI-enabled remote sensing reveals two urban rooftop PV adoption pathways: household vs. large-roof
abstract: Urban rooftop photovoltaics (RPV) offer a major decarbonization opportunity, yet cross-city, building-resolved evidence on adoption dynamics remains limited. We develop an AI-enabled remote-sensing framework that combines multi-temporal very-high-resolution aerial imagery with cadastral building footprints to map time-stamped RPV installations across New York City, Seattle, Phoenix, Singapore, and Zurich (2743 km2; mid-2000s-2024). A domain-adapted Vision Transformer segmentation model achieves a mean pixel-level intersection-over-union of 0.82 and building-level precision of 0.95 (F1 of 0.92) across cities. By linking segmentation-derived RPV area to individual buildings and PV-suitable roof area, we identify two recurring building-type pathway tendencies: a household-led pathway tendency in the three U.S. cities and a large-roof-oriented pathway tendency in Singapore and Zurich. These pathways are interpreted as associations shaped by roof-stock composition, tenure, governance, project economics, and policy design, rather than as direct causal effects of a single instrument. In the U.S. cities, model-based scenario attribution suggests that lagged adoption dynamics reduce projected 2028 single-residential adoption by 4.3, 1.3, and 1.7 percentage points in New York, Phoenix, and Seattle, respectively, while modeled net-cost shocks reduce adoption by 2.0, 0.5, and 0.3 percentage points. Because OBBB was enacted in 2025 and no post-OBBB adoption outcomes are available in the study period, these projections are forward-looking sensitivity exercises under unobserved policy conditions, not empirically observed policy responses or validated forecasts. The results indicate that urban RPV strategies should combine household-oriented programs with carefully designed large-roof programs while accounting for local institutional transferability, remaining roof headroom, and equity impacts.

title: Reaction network evolution and dynamic hydrogen redistribution in PAN stabilization revealed by machine learning potential-driven molecular dynamics
abstract: This study employs machine learning potential (MLP)-driven molecular dynamics simulations to investigate cyclization and dehydrogenation during the thermal stabilization of polyacrylonitrile (PAN) precursors based on acrylonitrile/methacrylic acid (AN/MAA) copolymer at the atomistic level. Thermally accelerated simulations combined with multi-model analysis reveal that PAN stabilization proceeds through a complex reaction network involving multiple competing cyclization pathways, including 6-membered rings, 5-membered rings, and C–C coupling-driven structures. Backtracking analysis across independent models enables systematic reconstruction of reaction pathways, which are classified into four distinct mechanisms based on bond formation and ring topology. The reaction is further interpreted in terms of cyclization initiation and propagation. During sequential heating, propagation becomes increasingly prevalent as cyclic structures accumulate, indicating that subsequent structural evolution is dominated by ring extension within the present activated models. In addition, dehydrogenation is shown to proceed not as simple hydrogen loss, but as a dynamic hydrogen redistribution process involving continuous bond rearrangement. These findings indicate that, once cyclic sites are formed, the subsequent structural evolution is dominated by propagation-driven network evolution in the present activated models. This work demonstrates that MLP based simulations provide a powerful framework for resolving complex, multi-pathway reaction mechanisms in polymer stabilization processes at the atomic scale.

title: Normal/inverse sandwich structure series-engineered multilayer double-atom catalysts featuring bridge-bonded dual-sulfur ligands: Machine learning-driven optimization for oxygen evolution/reduction reaction bifunctional electrocatalysts
abstract: Although a graphene-like carbon nitride monolayer (N4@g-C16N3) supported transition metal (TM) has been confirmed to possess excellent oxygen evolution/reduction reaction (OER/ORR) activity, we believe that certain modulation strategies can release significant potential for further enhancement. As such, we explored the potential of multilayer normal/inverse sandwich structures series derived from N4@g-C16N3 with dual-sulfur bridging for OER/ORR applications using density functional theory (DFT) and machine learning (ML). Initially, by comparing 27 double-atom catalysts (TMN4-S2-TMN4) dwelled in bilayer homonuclear normal sandwich structures with 27 single-atom catalysts ((TM-N4)@g-C16N3), confirming increased activities in bilayer systems and six high-activity TM-atoms stand out, leading to the generation of 183 bilayer normal/inverse sandwich structures. Orbital population analysis revealed that altering active metal atoms to synergize with dual-sulfur bridging layers can significantly impact bond order to optimize adsorption free energy (ΔGO*), a key descriptor for OER/ORR overpotentials. Subsequently, we employed an update bond order scheme to describe O* adsorption strength, introducing bond order corrections by analyzing bonding/antibonding electrons correlation with ΔGO*, thereby enhancing the scheme’s capability to describe OER/ORR activity and further explaining its origins. Under this framework, FeN4-S2-AgN4 exhibits the most suitable metal-O* interaction, demonstrated by excellent bifunctional performance. Based on 181 bilayer structures, we performed ML predictions on 548 others and validated the results using DFT. Additionally, constant-potential simulations reveal that the electric double layer plays a regulatory role in modulating reaction barriers, while the adsorption free energies, governed by both pH and electrode potential, underscore the excellent OER/ORR catalytic performance across a wide pH spectrum. By constructing simplified structural descriptors (φ), we labeled microenvironment changes around active sites caused by varying layer numbers and metal combinations, improving model’s generalizability and extended predictions for OER/ORR overpotentials to pseudo-bilayer and bi/tri/quadlayer sandwich systems (2,916 configurations), validated by DFT calculations. Meanwhile, formation energy predictions guarantee that these structures possess high thermal stability, supporting their practical feasibility.

title: Machine learning–assisted discovery of chromium bis(2-pyridyl)amine catalysts for ethylene tri-/tetramerization
abstract: The selective production of 1-hexene and 1-octene through chromium-catalyzed ethylene oligomerization remains a central challenge in catalyst design. In this work, we developed a fully automated, data-driven workflow to investigate the chromium bis(2-pyridyl)amine (Cr/NNN) catalytic system. A virtual database of 256 ligands with systematically varied R1-R3 substituents was constructed, and the relative transition-state Gibbs free energy differences (ΔΔG) between trimerization and tetramerization pathways were computed using DFT. To efficiently represent the key structural and physicochemical characteristics of the catalysts, molecular descriptors were extracted using SMILES-based structure generation combined with xTB calculations and RDKit-derived structural analysis. The developed machine learning models exhibited excellent predictive performance, achieving an R2 of 0.90 and a remarkably low MAE of 0.52 kcal/mol. Subsequent SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis identified the key structural features governing ΔΔG, confirming that the selectivity is primarily controlled by local steric effects at R1, with distant electronic substitutions contributing only weakly. Guided by the machine learning and SHAP analyses, two Cr/NNN catalysts were identified from the DFT-calculated dataset as optimal prototypes, showing exclusive selectivity for 1-hexene and 1-octene formation, respectively. This data-driven strategy can be readily extended to other transition-metal catalytic systems, offering a general framework for accelerating catalyst discovery and selectivity optimization.

title: Microkinetic modeling of methane activation in Mo/ZSM-5 with machine learning potentials
abstract: Mo/ZSM-5 catalyzes methane dehydroaromatization (MDA), yet the role of entropy on reactive intermediates and transition states remain unresolved. At reaction temperatures of 1000 K, the entropic contributions to the Gibbs free energy of reactive intermediates and transition states are challenging to model and can have consequences for predicting reaction kinetics and steady state coverages. The structure and distribution of active sites during MDA turnovers is complex and here we investigate the simplest ion-exchanged Mo carbide active site in ZSM-5 to isolate how entropy models affect methane activation. We consider two pathways: a C–C coupling pathway that forms ethylene after sequential methane dehydrogenation, and a MoC regeneration pathway that directly forms ethylene then reconstitutes [MoC]2+ sites. The harmonic oscillator approximation and partition function methods that assign hindered translational and rotational motions to low frequency modes were used to compute entropies at 1000 K. We then applied molecular dynamics using a machine learned potential (MLP) to obtain activation free energies for methane activation and hydrogen association via well-tempered metadynamics. Monte Carlo integration using an MLP was used to explicitly calculate translational and rotational entropy contributions for adsorbed methane. By comparing different entropy models, we demonstrate that translational and rotational modes are necessary for weakly adsorbed intermediates. Mean-field microkinetic modeling was used to quantify reaction orders and apparent activation energies for different entropy approximations. On this mononuclear MoC site, C–C coupling of unsaturated carbon intermediates is kinetically favored for direct ethylene formation, and the apparent kinetics depend on the entropy model. This manuscript demonstrates how MLPs in conjunction with enhanced sampling and Monte Carlo integration can inform entropy approaches in a reaction network to be integrated into microkinetic models.

title: Integrating DFT and machine learning for a dual-descriptor strategy in Gold(I) catalyst design: π-bond activation and orbital interactions
abstract: Interpretable understanding of ligand effects remains a key challenge in homogeneous gold(I) catalysis, particularly for reactions in which experimentally optimized systems already display high performance. Here, we combine density functional theory and interpretable machine learning (ML) to map ligand effects in Au(I)-catalyzed [2 + 2] cycloadditions of aryl alkynes and alkenes. A diverse set of 100 phosphine ligands was evaluated by DFT, and ensemble ML models trained on physically motivated descriptors reveal clear structure–reactivity relationships. The analysis consistently identifies the experimentally employed ligand as residing within the near-optimal region of the predicted activity–selectivity landscape, with closely related ligands occupying progressively less favorable regions. Targeted experimental comparisons and additional DFT calculations on representative ligands confirm these predicted trends and show that ligand variation does not induce a turnover-limiting step shift within the explored chemical space. These results provide an experimentally supported mapping of attainable ligand effects and intrinsic performance boundaries in this Au(I)-catalyzed system, highlighting the value of boundary-aware, interpretable machine learning approaches for understanding established gold catalysis.

title: Suppressing nanoparticle aggregation via engineered surface separation walls: a machine learning–driven molecular dynamics and experimental study
abstract: Enhancing the thermal stability of supported metal nanoparticles at high temperatures remains a significant challenge. The efficacy of constructing surface separation walls in mitigating nanoparticle aggregation was evaluated through complementary molecular dynamics simulations and experiments. Using machine learning potential, the effects of separation wall sizes including height, width, length and nanoparticle diameters on the aggregation behavior of Fe nanoparticles supported on Al2O3 surfaces were investigated. For separation walls of infinite length, increasing either the height or width consistently suppresses aggregation of Fe nanoparticles of given diameters. However, for walls of finite length, simply increasing the height is not always effective, as nanoparticles can migrate around the ends of walls. In the case of infinitely long walls, the height-to-diameter ratio determines the onset of aggregation. This critical ratio exhibits a negative correlation with the wall width. Finally, experiments clearly demonstrated the effectiveness of separation walls in enhancing Fe nanoparticles’ high-temperature stability. Finally, the simulations and experiments together reveal a system-dependent synergistic stabilization mechanism for Fe/Al2O3, in which geometric confinement by the separation walls and defect-/interface-mediated metal–support interactions act in concert; the critical height-to-diameter ratio derived from the atomistic simulations is intended as a qualitative design guideline rather than a universal quantitative threshold.

title: Interpretable machine learning-guided identification of C/H/O affinity descriptors for CO2-to-CH4 electrocatalysis on doped Cu surfaces
abstract: The electroreduction of carbon dioxide (CO2) to methane (CH4) over copper (Cu)-based catalysts is a promising route for sustainable fuel production. However, the reaction mechanism remains under debate because competing pathways can proceed through the key *COH and *CHO intermediates. Herein, we constructed 1,331 Cu-based catalyst models containing up to three metal and/or nonmetal dopants and employed CHGNet to rapidly evaluate the energetics of reaction intermediates along the COH and CHO pathways. By correlating key intermediate adsorption energies and the reaction-energy change of the limiting step (ΔElim) with surface C/H/O affinities, we elucidate their distinct roles in CH4 formation. Most doped Cu surfaces exhibit a thermodynamic preference for the CHO pathway over the COH pathway. H-affinity predominantly influences the adsorption energetics of key intermediates, whereas O-affinity strongly affects the limiting reaction-energy requirement for CH4 formation by modulating ΔElim. In the investigated catalyst space, dopants with higher d-electron counts tend to weaken O affinity and thereby reduce ΔElim. In contrast, C-affinity shows a comparatively limited correlation with intermediate adsorption energetics and ΔElim. These findings clarify how surface C/H/O affinities regulate CH4-forming pathways and provide design principles for Cu-based electrocatalysts with favorable CH4 formation energetics.

title: Mechanistic insights and structure–reactivity relationships of Ru(II)–Imidazole complex catalysts for formic acid dehydrogenation: A combined DFT and machine learning study
abstract: Formic acid dehydrogenation is a key reaction for hydrogen storage and release, and understanding its catalytic mechanism and structure–activity relationship is crucial for catalyst design. Here, DFT calculations were combined with machine learning (ML) to investigate ruthenium–imidazole amine complexes for formic acid dehydrogenation. DFT results show that the reaction preferentially occurs through the γ-N proton-responsive site via a stepwise pathway, with β-hydride elimination as the rate-determining step (ΔG≠ = 21.4 kcal/mol, relative to the resting state B-Int2), while the α-N pathway has a higher barrier (ΔG≠ = 33.4 kcal/mol, relative to B-Int2). Distortion/interaction analysis and IGMH analysis reveal that the superior activity of the γ-N pathway mainly originates from lower structural distortion energy and reduced steric repulsion, indicating distortion energy as the dominant factor controlling transition-state stability. Based on DFT data, an ML dataset including different metal centers (Ru, Fe, Os) and ligand substituents was constructed. Among eight regression models, the gradient boosting model showed the best performance (test R2 = 0.808, RMSE = 1.295 kcal/mol). SHAP analysis identified metal charge (qM) as the dominant descriptor, highlighting the importance of electronic effects. Further analysis revealed a volcano-shaped relationship between the HOMO–LUMO energy gap (Egap) and the reaction barrier, identifying an optimal Egap window (≈2.96 eV) where the barrier is minimized, underscoring that balanced electronic modulation is essential for high catalytic performance. These findings provide mechanistic insights into dual-proton-responsive sites and guide the rational design of efficient formic acid dehydrogenation catalysts.

title: Metal-organic frameworks based electrocatalysts for oxygen evolution: electrochemical fundamentals, structure-activity relations, and AI-guided design
abstract: Electrochemical water splitting is a key technology for sustainable hydrogen production, yet its large-scale application is hindered by the sluggish kinetics of the oxygen evolution reaction (OER). Noble-metal-based catalysts can effectively lower OER overpotentials, while their high cost, limited abundance, and durability issues motivate the development of alternative catalyst platforms. Metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) have emerged as a distinctive class of materials for OER catalysis because they integrate molecular-level coordination environments with extended porous architectures. Their modular metal nodes, tunable organic ligands, and defect-engineering capability enable precise regulation of local electronic structure, active-site density, and mass and charge transport. In addition, MOFs serve as structurally programmable precursors that can be transformed into catalytically active (oxy)hydroxides, oxides, and metal-carbon composites, allowing the transfer of well-defined coordination motifs into robust working catalysts. However, the immense compositional and structural diversity of MOF-based systems have caused empirical optimization inefficient. Artificial intelligence (AI) is therefore emerging as a complementary methodology that links synthesis, structure, and performance through data-driven machine learning. By combining physically informed descriptors with statistical models, AI-assisted approaches provide new opportunities to rationalize catalyst evolution and accelerate application-oriented discovery. This review summarizes recent advances in MOF-based and MOF-derived OER electrocatalysts, with an emphasis on structure-performance relationships and AI-guided design strategies. Current challenges and future directions toward practically deployable OER catalysts are discussed.

title: Imidazole-based MOFs for photo/electrocatalytic CO2 conversion: Controllable construction, mechanistic investigation, and machine learning
abstract: Imidazole-based MOFs, by virtue of the Lewis basicity endowed by electron-rich N sites, the Lewis acidity provided by tunable metal nodes, and the excellent designability of their pore structures, are ideal platforms for achieving highly active and highly selective photo/electrocatalytic conversion of CO2. This review systematically summarizes the latest progress of imidazole-based MOFs (including ZIFs, BIFs, and HZIFs) in the CO2RR. In terms of construction strategies, the structure-activity relationships are systematically elucidated from two dimensions: ligand engineering (functional group modification, coordination mode regulation, and defect engineering) and metal active site design (single-metal sites and heterometallic synergistic/cascade catalysis). It further covers multiscale functionalization pathways such as compositing with functional materials, carrier loading, and the preparation of derived materials. Regarding mechanistic research, by integrating in situ experimental characterizations and DFT calculations, the microscopic mechanisms of CO2 adsorption, activation, and multi-electron reduction are deeply revealed. Furthermore, it introduces the emerging applications of machine learning in high-throughput catalyst screening and reverse structural design. Finally, targeting core bottlenecks such as insufficient intrinsic conductivity, lack of device integration, and relatively high scale-up costs, it proposes future research directions for multidimensional synergistic breakthroughs, with the hope of driving the practical application of imidazole-based MOFs in the context of carbon neutrality.

title: MetaGNSDformer: Meta-learning enhanced gated non-stationary informer with frequency-aware attention for point-interval remaining useful life prediction of lithium-ion batteries
abstract: Remaining useful life (RUL) prediction of Lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) is essential for safe and reliability management of battery energy storage system (BESS). However, existing methods often overlook uncertainty quantification. Given the inherent uncertainty in LIBs degradation, especially under limited data, point predictions alone are insufficient for effective decision support. To tackle these, an end-to-end point-interval framework is proposed, comprising base learner and meta learner. The base learner, termed the GNSDformer, integrates Gated Non-stationary Informer with Discrete Cosine Transformation (DCT)-based Frequency Enhanced Channel Attention Mechanism (FECAM). Specially, Gated mechanism is employed to extract temporal features, while De-stationary ProbSparse Attention and FECAM block jointly enhance detection of non-stationary data dependencies and frequency information. Subsequently, MetaGNSDformer extends GNSDformer by incorporating an Eigen Reptile-based meta learner, which updates meta-parameters along the principal direction derived from source tasks. Through comprehensive experiments across LIBs from NASA datasets with small training samples, the effectiveness of each component within the MetaGNSDformer is demonstrated. Specifically, the model significantly outperforms existing point/interval prediction models. Furthermore, the Modified Diebold-Mariano test confirms the superiority of the MetaGNSDformer, while its stability is substantiated through repeated predictions. Hence, the proposed model has practical applicability in enhancing the safety and economic efficiency of BESS, thereby contributing to environmental sustainability.

title: Physics-informed deep learning method for surface roughness prediction in milling process
abstract: Surface roughness is critical to the functionality and aesthetic performance of mechanical components, necessitating precise prediction and control during the milling process. However, physics-based methods and data-driven methods either exhibit poor performance or lack interpretability, limiting their practical application. To address the issues, this article proposes a novel physics-informed deep learning (PIDL) for milling surface roughness prediction. The core idea is to leverage the principles of cutting mechanics and surface roughness to guide the model construction and regulate the network learning process. Firstly, a high-fidelity dynamic milling force model is established to generate simulated force signals for multi-sensor fusion with other measured signals. Then, the output of the surface roughness physical model is used as physics-guided knowledge to construct an attention-enhanced BiLSTM-BiGRU network based on cross physics-data fusion. In addition, a physics-informed loss function is designed to guide model training, thereby enhancing prediction performance and interpretability. The feasibility and superiority of the proposed method are validated through a series of milling tests under varying conditions. The results indicate that the proposed PIDL can achieve accurate surface roughness prediction in complex milling scenarios, with a coefficient of determination of 0.9845, a root mean square error of 0.0350, a mean absolute percentage error of 1.2895%, and a mean absolute error of 0.0284, outperforming both physics-based methods and data-driven methods.

title: Integrated machine learning framework for performance-based seismic assessment of post-tensioned steel-timber hybrid frames with energy-dissipating braces
abstract: Performance-based seismic assessment (PBSA) is essential for evaluating both structural safety and post-earthquake recovery. While machine learning (ML) has been used to predict seismic responses, its integration into full PBSA workflows—particularly for loss and downtime estimation—remains limited. This study formalizes a streamlined, building-specific ML-PBSA framework and demonstrates its application to post-tensioned steel–timber hybrid (PTSTH) frames with energy-dissipating braces. Seismic input uncertainty was addressed using Latin hypercube sampling and ground motion selection by return period. Feature engineering and ML algorithms were jointly optimized via tree-based Bayesian method. Surrogate models achieved high predictive accuracy (R2 = 0.940–0.966) for key response parameters, with a 95th percentile model improving upper-bound prediction of residual inter-story drift. Fragility analysis confirmed the suitability of ML outputs for damage assessment. The ML models were further integrated into the full PBSA process, including seismic loss and downtime estimation. Results closely matched those from nonlinear time history analysis, with prediction errors under 5 % for seismic events with 975-year return periods or longer.

title: Meta-learning-aided generalized anomaly detection for unmanned aerial vehicles from simulation to unseen reality
abstract: Anomaly detection is critical to the safety and reliability of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs). However, traditional deep learning methods rely on independent and identically distributed (i.i.d.) assumptions and are susceptible to data distribution variations, while domain adaptation approaches are constrained by privacy and data collection costs, making it difficult to obtain target data in advance or may be inaccessible. This paper introduces a novel meta-learning-aided generalized anomaly detection (Meta-GAD) framework, which harnesses knowledge acquired from multiple simulated domains to enable robust UAV anomaly detection in real-world scenarios. First, a local–global feature joint modeling method based on one-dimensional convolutional neural network and convolutional block attention module (1D CNN-CBAM) is constructed, which leverages 1D CNN for extraction of local features and adaptively fuses local–global information via CBAM’s channel- and spatial-attention mechanisms, enhancing the model’s ability to fit complex UAV flight data. Second, a model-agnostic meta-learning (MAML) approach with a dual-gradient optimization strategy is designed, leveraging the 1D CNN-CBAM model as the base learner to learn domain-invariant representation via two gradient updates in inner-outer loops. Then, an adaptive detection strategy integrating anomaly feature enhancement and extreme distribution modeling is introduced to improve the performance of anomaly detection. Finally, the efficacy of the proposed framework is validated through model training on multiple simulated flight datasets and model testing on an unseen real flight dataset.

title: Autonomous component optimization method for steel braced frame structures based on multi-agent and physics-informed deep reinforcement learning
abstract: Steel braced frame structures have gained widespread adoption. However, the design process is complex and heavily reliant on expert knowledge and iterative trial-and-error methods, making it time-consuming and labor-intensive. To address these challenges, this paper proposes an innovative autonomous method, namely FrameMARL, which integrates Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) into the design process of steel braced frame structures. FrameMARL decouples the steel braced frame into multiple sub-frames and utilizes a multi-agent system (FrameMAS) to design the components across different floors independently. Through computer experiments, it is demonstrated that FrameMAS can efficiently design steel braced frame aligning with safety and economics requirements, and it outperforms the single-agent method (FrameSA) in both the quality of the design and material usage efficiency. In addition, a 3D practical case study validates the feasibility and efficiency of FrameMARL in real-world applications, showcasing its potential to streamline the design process for complex structures.

title: Physics-constrained deep symbolic regression for efficient design of aerial building machine
abstract: Aerial building machine (ABM) is an innovative large-scale construction equipment designed for high-rise buildings. It offers construction workers a secure and solid platform at significant heights. The existing ABM design methodology is predicated upon a substantial dependence on expert knowledge and experience, with the features of time-consuming, inefficient, and conservative. This study proposes an automated approach to optimize the layout design of ABM based on deep symbolic regression (DSR), parametric modeling, and multi-objective optimization (MOO). Specifically, a multi-software co-simulation environment is first utilized to establish a structural response dataset for the critical components of ABM. Subsequently, a physics-constrained deep symbolic regression (PCDSR) algorithm is proposed to explore structural mechanics characteristics and develop a simplified model of ABM. Lastly, an automated optimization framework integrating parametric modeling and MOO is constructed to achieve the intelligent and efficient layout design of ABM. This approach has been verified in a real construction project using ABM in China. The results indicate: (1) The formulas generated from the PCDSR can accurately predict and explain the mechanical characteristics of the Bailey truss, where the R2 of the formulas is above 0.97. (2) The optimal scheme saves 20.38% in steel consumption and reduces 49.76% on average in structural deformation compared to the existing scheme. (3) The comparison experiment demonstrates a 60.90% enhancement in training efficiency when incorporating physical variable constraints into the DSR algorithm. The scientific contributions lie in the integration of physical variable constraints into DSR, thereby facilitating an intelligent design framework for the efficient layout design of ABM. The study demonstrates the potential of intelligent design technology to enhance design efficiency, optimize spatial layouts, and promote human–machine collaboration in the ABM design process.

title: Physics-informed graph transformer network for predicting cable-stayed bridge structural deflection response
abstract:
Accurately predicting the deflection response of complex structures such as cable-stayed bridges remains a significant challenge. To address this, this study proposes a physics-informed graph transformer network (PiGTN). The PiGTN leverages a physics-informed adjacency matrix derived from structural mechanics to encode sensor dependencies. An enhanced graph convolutional network (GCN) with second-order convolution captures spatial correlations, while a transformer encoder models temporal dynamic. The training process employs a mixed loss function that integrates data-driven loss with physical “soft constraints” from the Euler-Bernoulli beam solution, ensuring predictions conform to physical laws.
The effectiveness of the PiGTN was validated on a real-world bridge, demonstrating significantly higher prediction accuracy than state-of-the-art spatiotemporal models. In challenging and extreme scenarios, outstanding stability and accuracy are exhibited by the PiGTN, underscoring the robustness provided by its physical information. Ablation experiments quantified each component’s contribution, revealing that the removal of physical information, the Transformer encoder, and the enhanced graph convolution each led to a notable degradation in model performance. Additionally, the parameter sensitivity analysis provides guidance for model tuning and deployment. A high-precision, robust, and interpretable deep learning (DL) model is introduced in this study, providing a novel solution for bridge structural health monitoring (SHM).

title: Bayesian physics-informed neural networks with iterative ensemble Kalman inversion for RUL prediction and uncertainty quantification
abstract: Precise and dependable remaining useful life (RUL) estimation plays a vital role in ensuring effective operation and maintenance of industrial machinery. In recent years, the performance of RUL prediction has been greatly enhanced owing to the ability of physics-informed neural networks (PINN) to incorporate underlying physical degradation mechanisms into deep learning frameworks. However, the inherent physical constraints of PINN make it difficult to accurately quantify RUL uncertainty using Bayesian approximate inference sampling methods. Consequently, PINN-based machine RUL prediction models struggle to quantify RUL uncertainty, resulting in reduced confidence in the predicted RUL. To address these issues, we propose an iterative ensemble Kalman inversion-based (IEKI) Bayesian PINN (BPINN) to estimate RUL and uncertainty within mechanical systems. First, a deep physical-information network is constructed to learn the latent deterioration characteristics of the mechanical system, where the data loss is regularized by a physical residual term to optimize model parameters. Then, a deep integration of the Bayesian neural network and PINN is conducted to form a Bayesian PINN capable of uncertainty quantification. Finally, an efficient inference strategy based on iterative ensemble Kalman inversion is designed to estimate the posterior over network parameters within the BPINN framework. Extensive experiments are conducted on the C-MAPSS, N-CMAPSS, and nuclear circulating water pump (NCWP) datasets to validate the effectiveness and advantages of the proposed method, indicating improved performance in evaluating machine RUL and its associated uncertainty.

title: PIFL: Physics-informed federated learning for progressive degradation estimation in energy storage devices
abstract: Accurate estimation of the health in energy storage devices, such as batteries, is essential for enhancing system safety and reliability. Deep learning methods effectively capture nonlinearities in battery monitoring sequences, while federated learning approaches improve generalization by aggregating knowledge from distributed devices. However, these approaches usually overlook latent environmental influences, inherent physical constraints, and data heterogeneity arising from diverse operating conditions. To overcome these limitations, we propose a Physics-Informed Federated Learning (PIFL) framework, which integrates a Pattern-aware Gated Recurrent Unit (PGRU) network, a Physics-constrained Learning (PL) module, and a Physics-Informed Federated Strategy (PIFS). The PGRU progressively learns the interactions between temporal degradation information and latent environmental factors (e.g., temperature), thereby optimizing feature representation. The PL module embeds degradation-related physical constraints into the network to enforce physically consistent predictions. The PIFS component introduces a degradation-aware model selection strategy and an attention-based aggregation mechanism, improving adaptability under diverse conditions. Experiments conducted on eight cases across four public datasets demonstrate that PIFL consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods in accuracy, generalization, and convergence speed. Moreover, the proposed framework exhibits strong potential for broader application in industrial contexts.

title: A fault diagnosis strategy for gearboxes based on reinforcement learning with balanced reward and cost- equilibrium sampling
abstract: To address the challenge of deep reinforcement learning exhibiting low accuracy in data-imbalanced gearbox fault diagnosis, this paper proposes a Reinforcement Learning Model with Cost-sensitive Sampling and Balanced Reward (RLM-CSBR) from the perspectives of feature representation, data utilization, and learning strategy. To tackle the lack of minority-class feature patterns, a multi-level convolutional deep integrated Q-network is constructed to fully explore deep discriminative features from imbalanced data, thereby maximizing feature-perceptive information. To mitigate model training bias, a balanced reward strategy based on the sample missing rate is designed; this strategy not only guides the agent to prioritize the exploration and learning of sample-scarce categories but also ensures the utilization efficiency of majority-class samples. To solve the problem of insufficient model fitting for minority-class samples, a novel cost-equilibrium matrix is incorporated into the prioritized experience replay mechanism, which prioritizes the selection of high-value experiences learned from critical minority-class samples during training.

title: Generalizable dynamics modeling of serial robotic manipulators via a Lagrangian dynamics neural network with mechanism priors
abstract: As one of the most widely adopted and reliable robot architectures in modern manufacturing, serial robotic manipulators play a critical role in key production tasks such as welding, polishing, grinding, and human–robot collaborative assembly. To address the growing demands for precision, stability, safety, and adaptability in manufacturing systems, it is essential to develop a robot dynamics model that is accurate, efficient, and generalizable across diverse tasks and environments. Purely physics-based modeling methods often struggle with accuracy due to nonlinear factors such as friction and elasticity. In contrast, data-driven approaches can capture complex nonlinear dynamics directly from data but typically exhibit poor extrapolation and limited interpretability. To address these challenges, this paper proposes the Lagrangian Dynamics Neural Network (LagDNN), which embeds physical priors into the neural network architecture based on the principles of robot dynamics. By structuring the model in accordance with Lagrangian dynamics, LagDNN improves the extrapolation and generalization capabilities of data-driven models while enabling accurate inverse dynamics modeling for serial manipulators. LagDNN comprises three physics-informed submodules—Inertial Net, Gravity Net, and Friction Net—each responsible for modeling a distinct component of the robot’s dynamics. Experimental evaluations on simulated robots, the UR5 robotic arm, and the WAM cable-driven robotic arm demonstrate that LagDNN achieves superior accuracy and efficiency in inverse dynamics modeling. Furthermore, it exhibits strong generalization beyond the training distribution, underscoring its robustness and practical applicability.

title: Physics-informed reinforcement learning for air-to-air F16 target aiming
abstract: Due to the unstable aircraft dynamics and variable flying conditions, the design of flight control and guidance law have been a challenging task. To address the issue, this paper has proposed a hybrid strategy for aircraft target aiming control, Reinforcement Learning-based Gain Tuning Approximate Posture Incremental Control (RLGT-APIC). Based on the rule-based control framework, approximate posture incremental control (APIC), the proposed strategy uses RL agent to adaptively tune the controller gains, which improves the environment robustness. To validate the effectiveness of the proposed method, the paper applies JSBSim to simulate the flight control and uses F-16 fighter as the control system. The simulation results prove that the RL based adaptive gain tuning network can exhibit better target aiming performance compared to the conventional APIC. The proposed method not only provides a robust RL targeting control for aircrafts, but also offers a sample-efficient learning framework for RL agent to learn flight control tasks.

title: Physics-informed spatiotemporal architecture in digital twin modeling for condition monitoring of aircraft engines
abstract: Condition monitoring is pivotal in ensuring the safety and reliability of aircraft engines. Digital twin (DT) technology builds an interactive bridge between digital and physical spaces, offering benefits in real-time condition monitoring and fault prognostics. This study proposes a novel physics-informed spatiotemporal modeling framework for aircraft engine DT, integrating domain-specific physical knowledge, transformer-based feature learning, and transfer learning. The architecture comprises two core components: (1) temporal feature encoders with causal attention mechanisms to capture component-specific operational patterns while preserving temporal causality, and (2) a spatial coupling module employing bidirectional attention to model inter-component interactions based on the engine’s physical topology. To improve computational efficiency, we further introduce a temporal-transfer paradigm that leverages pretrained temporal encoders to generate generalized temporal features, which are then fed into task-specific spatial modules for localized learning—reducing substantial computational costs without sacrificing accuracy. Validation on three operational datasets demonstrated that the proposed method achieves optimized mean absolute percentage errors (MAPE) of 0.5%, 0.3%, and 2% for 𝐹 (thrust), 𝑃3 (total pressure at high-pressure compressor outlet), and 𝐸⁢𝐺⁡𝑇 (exhaust gas temperature) predictions, respectively, representing reductions of 43.9–79.8%, 41.9–87.3%, and 12.1–25.0% compared with temporal-only, spatial-only attention and long short-term memory (LSTM)-based baselines. By integrating causal-temporal attention mechanisms and physics-guided spatial coupling, the proposed framework not only ensures high prediction precision but also reduces computational costs through temporal feature transfer. This dual capability addresses the critical requirements of high-fidelity simulation and real-time responsiveness for industrial DT deployments.
