title: A physics-informed neural network approach for random vibration analysis of train-bridge system via probability density evolution equation
abstract: To address the high computational cost and numerical stability constraints of conventional finite-difference solvers for the probability density evolution equation (PDEE) in train-bridge system (TBS) stochastic vibration analysis, this study proposes a physics-informed neural network (PINN)-based framework. A train-bridge coupled dynamic model is first established, and the governing equation of motion and the corresponding PDEE are derived. These two equations serve fundamentally different purposes, with the equation of motion governing the deterministic system response and the PDEE describing the probability evolution of that response. Then, the PDEE, together with initial and boundary conditions, is embedded into the PINN loss via automatic differentiation, enabling a mesh-free solution for the time-dependent probability density function (PDF). Taking the stochastic dynamic response of a high-speed railway bridge as the target, the proposed method is validated against conventional probability density evolution method (PDEM) benchmark solutions. Numerical investigations under varying train speeds and random train-parameter conditions demonstrate that the method achieves high accuracy and stability in solving the PDEE. The main contributions are fourfold: (i) a physics-informed framework embedding the generalized PDEE into the network loss for mesh-free PDF evolution; (ii) a 42.7 % reduction in PDEE-solving cost versus finite-difference PDEM with maintained statistical accuracy; (iii) robustness across train speeds of 260–340 km/h and load coefficient of variation (CV) of 0.08–0.16; and (iv) accurate capture of non-Gaussian features and time-varying evolution for infrastructure reliability assessment.

title: A hybrid physics-informed neural network-crossformer framework for inversion of reservoir parameters in large-scale gas storage flow systems
abstract: Large-scale underground natural gas storage (UNGS) faces challenges such as drastic changes in injection-withdrawal rates and periodic cycling, which hinder traditional machine learning methods by reducing pressure prediction accuracy and reservoir parameter inversion reliability. To address this, this paper proposes a hybrid framework combining physics-informed neural networks with Crossformer model for high-accuracy transient pressure prediction in UNGS during the pressure build-up period. The model utilizes the preceding pressure and gas injection–withdrawal rates as input, and reservoir pressure as output. The cubic spline interpolation is utilized to handle data sparsity, and a moving window method is used to calculate pressure derivatives. By explicitly embedding the residuals of the reservoir flow governing equations into the loss function, the model is guided to learn patterns consistent with reservoir physics. A weighted abrupt change-point loss mechanism is introduced to enhance the model’s detection of abrupt changes. The whale optimization algorithm is employed for network and hyperparameters tuning. The framework achieves an early-stage mean squared error of 6.49 × 10-9 and a prediction accuracy of 99.98% after inverse normalization. The application in the real case of the Hutubi UNGS shows that the initial formation pressure is 31.78 MPa and the permeability is 11.64 mD.

title: A physics-informed dynamic transmission error-driven inversion network for few-shot gear spalling severity identification
abstract: Gear transmission systems may develop tooth surface spalling of varying severity during service. Beyond detecting the presence of a fault, identifying spalling severity provides more targeted information for condition assessment and maintenance. However, measured data covering different spalling severity levels are usually scarce in practical applications, which limits the training of data-driven severity identification models. Existing data generation methods face challenges in terms of physical fidelity and virtual-real consistency. To overcome these limitations, this paper proposes a physics-informed dynamic transmission error-driven inversion network (PI-DTEN) for few-shot gear spalling severity identification. First, by embedding a gear dynamic model into the neural network, PI-DTEN directly uses reconstructed in-situ dynamic transmission error (DTE) signals to drive the inversion of key dynamic parameters. Since DTE characterizes the in-situ relative motion error between the driving and driven gears, it is more directly related to the gear meshing process than housing vibration responses. Therefore, using reconstructed in-situ DTE as the observation can reduce the dependence on housing vibration signals and alleviate the influence of transfer-path attenuation and structural noise during parameter inversion. Second, a physically meaningful multi-constraint hybrid loss function, a physical normalization strategy, and a resonance-inspired spectral calibration strategy are integrated to improve the reliability of the identified parameters and the virtual-real consistency of the generated data. Finally, using the reliable physical parameters identified by PI-DTEN, additional virtual DTE samples for a healthy reference state and three prescribed spalling levels of 2.5%, 5%, and 7.5% are forward-generated and combined with the limited measured samples to train a standard 1D-CNN model. Experimental results on a gearbox test rig show that the proposed method achieves an average classification accuracy of 92.2%, indicating its effectiveness in supporting few-shot gear spalling severity identification.

title: Dual-path physics-informed heterogeneous information fusion for axial piston pump health assessment in construction machinery
abstract: Reliable health assessment of hydraulic power components is essential for autonomous construction machinery. As the core power component, the health of axial piston pumps directly impacts the safety of automated process. However, traditional single-source data-driven methods are limited by incomplete information and vulnerable to sensor malfunctions or data loss. To address this, we propose a dual-path physics-informed heterogeneous information fusion (DP-PIHIF) framework, which consists of a Virtual Health Indicator (VHI) path and a Physical Health Indicator (PHI) path, integrating high-frequency vibration and relatively low-frequency physical data. In the VHI path, multi-domain vibration features are extracted and compressed using a Variational Autoencoder to characterize dynamic fault signatures. In the PHI path, a Physics-Informed Transformer is developed to infer interpretable leakage-related coefficients from multi-sensor hydraulic measurements, with physical consistency enforced through a volumetric flow loss model. The resulting VHI and PHI representations are integrated using an adaptive heterogeneous fusion module with dynamic weight allocation, followed by a multi-task learning scheme for simultaneous health state classification and ordinal health-level regression. Experimental results show superior assessment accuracy and regression stability, outperforming single-source baselines. This indicates the promising potential of the proposed framework for remote health assessment, which may support the predictive maintenance and operational continuity in autonomous construction machinery.

title: 3D CSFM: Cross-domain adaptation of visual foundation models for 3D seismic fault segmentation
abstract: Three-dimensional seismic fault segmentation is a knowledge-intensive task in subsurface structural interpretation and hydrocarbon exploration. Yet scarce field annotations limit robustness across acquisition and processing conditions, while unlabeled seismic data lack the scale and diversity needed to train a fault-oriented foundation model from scratch. We therefore propose 3D CSFM, a cross-domain framework that adapts a pretrained vision foundation model (VFM) to 3D fault segmentation through three components. Inspired by the directional structures of seismic volumes, the Bidirectional 3D Feature Adaptation Encoder (Bi3DA-Encoder) employs complementary spatial-view and depth-view pathways to model within-slice fault extension and cross-slice offset variations, respectively, while embedding lightweight depthwise-separable 3D adapters into the pretrained 2D vision encoder to transform planar visual priors into direction-aware 3D fault representations without extensive fine-tuning. The Spatial Context-Aware Decoder (SCA-Decoder) uses multiscale 3D context aggregation and deep supervision to reconstruct continuous fault structures and delineate weak boundaries. To bridge the synthetic-to-field domain gap, cross-domain collaborative training couples a seismic-structure-aware VFM branch comprising the Bi3DA-Encoder and SCA-Decoder with a local-detail-sensitive 3D convolutional branch, dynamically fuses the branches’ complementary predictions to generate target-domain supervision, and applies consistency and discrepancy regularization to reduce pseudo-label error accumulation and confirmation bias. Trained with synthetic labels and unlabeled field data, 3D CSFM quantitatively outperforms baselines on the synthetic validation set and labeled Thebe field data. Qualitative results on F3 and the unseen Kerry and Poseidon surveys support its effectiveness on these specific surveys. The framework enables annotation-efficient seismic fault interpretation and VFM adaptation in knowledge-intensive geophysical workflows.

title: LLM-augmented progressive search for efficient multi-robot task planning
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) demonstrate potential in task planning, with a small portion of that work dedicated to multi-robot collaboration tasks. However, existing studies focus on using multiple LLMs engaging in collaborative dialogue to attempt to find good plans, while the efficiency of these plans remains uncertain due to hallucinations and inaccuracies exhibited by LLMs. To cope with this issue, we propose the Retrieval-augmented Progressive Search with LLMs (RePS-LLM), which is the first to introduce LLMs into search algorithms for reliably finding efficient action plans in multi-robot collaboration. More specifically, the LLM policy is assisted by retrieval-augmented generation to progressively add actions, biasing the search toward estimating the values of more promising actions. In addition, our method proposes a group selection strategy to constrain the progressive action selection, improving search efficiency by ensuring that the LLM adds feasible coordinating actions. Experimental evaluations indicate that RePS-LLM surpasses state-of-the-art LLM planning frameworks, yielding an average 46% increase in success rate and a 15% reduction in steps with more than 10 robots.

title: Chemical reaction neural networks for semi-detailed kinetic schemes including the influence of inorganics and secondary reactions during cellulose pyrolysis
abstract: The demand for renewable energy and chemicals is increasing and biomass, as one of the most important sources of renewable energy and green carbon, is attracting significant attention in recent years. To understand and model biomass pyrolysis, detailed kinetic schemes are necessary. Conventional kinetic analysis requires a lot of prior knowledge and chemical insights. Due to the complex processes involved in biomass pyrolysis, conventional kinetic analysis methods face noticeable challenges, especially when considering the heterogeneity of the material, the influence of inorganic species, and the coupling of transport limitations with chemical pathways. Benefiting from available experimental data and rapidly progressing machine-learning techniques, a data-driven method based on the chemical reaction neural network (CRNN) is employed in the present study to determine a new semi-detailed kinetic scheme for the pyrolysis of cellulose, accounting for the impact of inorganic species (potassium, K) and mild transport limitations. Experiments have been conducted with different initial masses (5 and 20 mg), heating rates (2.5, 5, and 10 K min−1), with/without K (catalyst), with/without lid (external transport limitations). The obtained kinetics are physically interpreted and finally validated against conventional data-fitting methods. The CRNN leads to a semi-detailed kinetic scheme for modeling purposes.

title: Designing resilience building for climate change adaptation (future climate and extreme daily heat event): machine learning and multi-objective algorithms for decreasing heat stress and energy efficiency
abstract: This research aims to design a residential building with the highest long-term adaptability from a climate change perspective. Addressing energy consumption factors, health, thermal comfort indices, indoor overheating, and heating risk indices. Therefore, we tackle the challenges involved in designing a residential building in Tehran. A framework has been developed using simulation software and computational techniques to predict the future impacts of climate change on buildings in Tehran. Then, the building’s adaptability to future climatic conditions and extreme daily heat events was calculated using predicted climate data, and an appropriate design was implemented. This research has increased the adaptability of residential buildings to future climate changes by employing climate-compatible architectural solutions, including adjustments to the infiltration, depth, and angle of sunshades, the number and model of louvers, thermal mass, material insulation, natural ventilation, and green roofs. Genetic algorithms and machine learning identified the most effective and practical scenarios. On the other hand, the sensitivity of each variable to climate change was determined. Results showed that the optimized model reduced Energy Use Intensity (EUI) by approximately 25 %, decreased Indoor Overheating Degree (IOhD) by 24 %, and maintained HI and Humidex within the thermal comfort range (4.7–5.5 °C and 18–21 °C, respectively) under future climates. Compared to the baseline, annual overheating hours declined by 36 %, while Predicted Percentage of Dissatisfied (PPD) remained below 6 %. The sensitivity analysis using SHAP identified shading angle as the most influential parameter.

title: A hybrid data-driven and physics-informed energy management model for electrical grids with spatio-temporal cyberattack detection-reconstruction using digital twin
abstract: This paper proposes a comprehensive framework for cyber-resilient optimal energy management system (EMS) in smart grids. A complete 24-hour closed-loop operational cycle is modeled and simulated. It begins with data measurement via a real-time updated nonlinear Digital Twin, followed by transmission through SCADA/RTUs, detection of cyberattacks, accurate reconstruction of corrupted data, and finally EMS. The outputs of EMS are then sent back to the Digital Twin, which is dynamically updated to reflect the actual network conditions and generate accurate synthetic measurements for the next hour. This entire process is embedded within a 24-hour rolling optimization scheme. The EMS includes a power flow model integrated with various distributed energy resources (DERs), such as renewables, diesel generator, battery, electric vehicle, and controllable loads. It also incorporates and ensures all technical, security, and dynamic constraints of the grid and DERs. Unlike previous studies that focus only on isolated aspects such as attack detection, data estimation, or day-ahead energy management, this work implements the entire process in a unified and dynamic framework. The model functions effectively in networks where PMUs are unavailable, as is the case in most real-world distribution grids, because it is designed solely based on RTU and SCADA data. Detection and reconstruction of coordinated attacks rely on physics-based recalculation methods, utilizing grid topology and data from neighboring buses to improve accuracy. The proposed model is validated on the IEEE 33-bus test system, successfully detecting various attack scenarios targeting different parameters, locations, and times. It reconstructs the correct values with high precision and optimizes the network operation accordingly. This 24-hour rolling simulation demonstrates the practicality and robustness of the approach in enabling secure, cost-effective, and resilient energy management in modern smart grids.

title: Harnessing the optimization strategy via interpretable machine learning framework for high-efficiency pyrolysis-catalysis engineering of plastic wastes
abstract: Conventional pyrolysis-catalysis recycling of plastic wastes into high-value and clean hydrogen relys on laborious trial-and-error protocol, facing challenge due to high-dimensional and nonlinear nature of catalyst and process optimization for hydrogen production. Accurate prediction of H2 production and systematic optimization of pyrolysis-catalysis is crucial for plastic wastes valorization. In this work, an interpretable machine learning framework integrating hierarchical data mining, model training, interpretability analysis and inverse optimization was leveraged to predict hydrogen production, simultaneously grasping the complex correlations between variables. Several advanced tree regressor models are developed using feedstock composition, catalyst properties and process parameters as input features. The results showed that random forest model demonstrated the highest predictive performance with R2 of 0.88 and RMSE of 9.78. The causal analytics using Shapley Additive exPlanations identified the significant features of steam flow, metal loading and catalyst-to-feedstock ratio on hydrogen prediction. Data mining and partial dependence analysis revealed that proper metal loading of around 15 wt% when paired with a steam flow rate of 5 g/h could effectively regulate catalytic process to achieve the desired H2 yield. Transition metal-based catalysts with moderate porosity of approximately 100 m2/g and pore volume of 0.2–0.3 cm3/g, as well as catalyst-to-feedstock ratio of 0.8 have the potential to promote enhanced hydrogen selectivity and favorable product distributions. By harnessing the machine learning techniques, the hierarchical data-driven approach endowed insights into the rational selection of catalyst, and the identification of optimal operational conditions for sustainable hydrogen production from plastic wastes.

title: Optimizing steam-to-carbon and air-to-carbon ratios in internal autothermal reforming of a biogas-fed solid oxide fuel cell using the combination of computational fluid dynamics and artificial intelligence
abstract: This study addresses the challenge of optimizing steam-to-carbon (S/C) and air-to-carbon (Air/C) ratios in auto thermal reforming (ATR) processes within biogas-fed solid oxide fuel cells (SOFCs), a key factor in maximizing performance while mitigating carbon deposition risks. Insufficient steam and air hinder internal reforming reactions, while excess steam and air dilute the fuel and reduce output power. In this study, a comprehensive three-dimensional numerical model is developed to investigate the effects of S/C and Air/C ratios on the performance of a biogas-fed SOFC undergoing autothermal reforming (ATR). Kinetic models are implemented using User-Defined Functions (UDFs) in ANSYS Fluent, capturing the complex interplay of exothermic and endothermic processes inside the cell. The simulation results reveal that increasing the S/C ratio up to 0.5 enhances hydrogen production through steam reforming (SR) and full steam reforming (FSR) reactions, boosting the current and power densities. However, further increases in S/C beyond 0.5 dilute the fuel mixture and diminish performance. Similarly, increasing the Air/C ratio to 0.5 improves temperature distribution and accelerates reforming reactions via the exothermic total combustion (TC) reaction, but higher Air/C ratios (>0.5) excessively consume methane, thereby limiting hydrogen production. Carbon deposition analysis using Gibbs triangle criteria demonstrated that very low S/C and Air/C ratios lead to thermodynamic conditions favorable to carbon formation, whereas optimal ratios maintain the system outside the carbon deposition zone. To further refine the optimization, an artificial neural network (ANN) was trained using simulation data to model the relationship between S/C, Air/C, and power density. Next, an unconstrained optimization algorithm was employed to determine the best S/C and Air/C values. This approach yielded optimal ratios of S/C = 0.4264 and Air/C = 0.3517, resulting in a maximum power density of 0.4584 W/cm2 an improvement of approximately 3 % over the best case identified through trial-and-error simulations.

title: Optimization of platinum distribution in low-humidity proton exchange membrane fuel cells via multiphysics-informed neural network
abstract: Platinum (Pt) catalysts play a crucial role in determining the cost, durability, and efficiency of low-humidity proton exchange membrane fuel cell (PEMFC). However, comprehensive studies on Three-Dimensional (3D) Pt distributions that integrate the advantages of multiple gradient types remain limited, primarily due to the challenges in modeling spatial anisotropy and the strong coupling among optimization parameters. To overcome this, a Multiphysics-Informed Neural Network (MINN) is developed as a surrogate model, facilitating efficient multi-objective optimization of 3D Pt distributions. A detailed PEMFC Multiphysics agglomerate model is constructed to enable the implementation of an anisotropic exponential (AEXP) Pt distribution. Unlike conventional isotropic designs, the AEXP architecture spatially tunes the local reaction rate, simultaneously boosting electrochemical efficiency and suppressing degradation. Subsequently, four critical Multiphysics performance indicators are extracted: oxygen distribution uniformity, water accumulation, high-power density region, and temperature uniformity. Furthermore, MINN decouples the relationship between these indicators and Pt distribution parameters. The AEXP parameters are then optimized using the Non-dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm II (NSGA-II), and the optimal low-humidity strategy is selected from the Pareto front using the Technique for Order Preference by Similarity to Ideal Solution (TOPSIS). Comparative analyses among three commonly used convex distribution types—Exponential, Inverse, and Quadratic—reveal that the Exponential function outperforms the others under low-humidity conditions, yielding enhanced power density and reduced non-uniformity. Compared with the commonly adopted Random distribution strategy, the proposed Pt distribution improves power density by 4.21 %, oxygen and thermal uniformity by 42.32 % and 0.58 %, respectively, and enhances water removal efficiency by 9.90 %. This study provides a new insight to high freedom Pt distribution optimization with high efficiency, durability and low cost.

title: Multi-objective design optimization of a CO2 gascooler for electric vehicle applications under all-climate conditions via the machine learning method
abstract: The adoption of CO2 as a refrigerant is rapidly increasing due to stricter environmental regulations, which has led to a growing interest in CO2-based heat pump systems for electric vehicles. Improving the efficiency of these systems requires optimizing the design of heat exchangers, particularly the gascooler, which plays a crucial role in heat rejection and absorption. In this study, a machine learning-based optimization framework was developed to improve the geometric design of a CO2 gascooler while reducing its pressure drop, weight, and volume. Experimental data and correlation-based calculations were used to construct a surrogate model that predicts the thermal and hydraulic performance of the gascooler. The surrogate model was trained using a neural network and coupled with a multi-objective genetic algorithm to optimize heat transfer rate, pressure drop, and mass simultaneously. A SHAP-based sensitivity analysis was also performed to interpret the contribution of each geometric parameter to the predicted performance and to identify the dominant design variables. Unlike previous studies that focused on a single operating mode, this work considered three representative operating conditions corresponding to summer, winter, and transitional climates. The optimized gascooler achieved up to 150 % increase in heat transfer performance, 32.7 % reduction in pressure drop, 59.0 % reduction in weight, and 45 % reduction in volume compared with baseline. System-level evaluation further confirmed that the optimized designs improved performance under both heating and cooling operations, demonstrating that all-climate optimization effectively enhances the overall performance of CO2 heat pump systems for electric vehicles.

title: A physics-informed neural network framework for state estimation of latent heat thermal energy storage: temperature reconstruction and state-of-charge prediction
abstract: Effective integration of latent heat thermal energy storage (LHTES) systems into energy networks requires rapid and accurate internal state estimation. While nonlinear observers enable fast state estimation, they are constrained by sampling and computational burden. Conventional artificial intelligence-based methods are promising yet typically data-intensive and physically inconsistent. To overcome this, a physics-informed state estimator (PI-SE) is proposed, combining a temperature-reconstructing physics-informed neural network (T-PINN) with a multilayer perceptron for state-of-charge (SOC) estimation (SOC-MLP). By embedding physical information into the learning process, the framework improves accuracy under limited data availability. The proposed loss function design and training strategy address phase-change-induced discontinuities and PINNs mismatch, enhancing training efficiency and robustness. On the test dataset, the proposed PI-SE framework achieves a mean absolute error of 0.317℃ in temperature field prediction and 0.246% in SOC estimation. Further investigations yield four key findings: (1) the PI-SE model exhibits robustness to variations in sampling intervals under simulated deployment conditions; (2) a moderately scaled deep-and-narrow network (seven layers, 30 neurons per layer) achieves the trade-off between accuracy and generalization; (3) T-PINN outperforms purely data-driven models in both temperature reconstruction and SOC prediction under data-scarce scenarios; and (4) a dataset size between 100 and 150 samples is sufficient for effective model construction, balancing predictive performance and computational cost. This work provides an initial demonstration of a PI-SE framework for LHTES and its potential applicability to real-time monitoring and future energy-management strategies.

title: Ai-driven optimization and engine evaluation of Palmyra biodiesel synthesized via cobalt chromite catalysis
abstract: The increasing demand for green energy solutions, supplemented by advancements in artificial intelligence, drives innovation in sustainable fuel technologies. The present study focuses on synthesizing biodiesel using palmyra seed extract via solvent extraction and transesterification, improved by a novel cobalt chromite (CoCr2O4) nanoparticle catalyst. It showed better thermal stability and eco-friendly while being more efficient than its conventional counterpart. To optimize three main process parameters-namely, catalyst concentration (CC), methanol-to-feedstock ratio (MOR), and reaction time (RT)-three predictive algorithms, namely XGBoost, GBM, and CatBoost, have been employed in this work. XGBoost emerged as the best among them, helping to guide the optimal yield prediction and process refinement. The prepared biodiesel was then tested in a compact mono-cylinder compression ignition setup with three different fueling combinations: pure petroleum diesel (D100), pure palmyra biodiesel (P100), and a 20% biodiesel blend (P20). Among these, P20 showed nearly diesel-like performance with a brake thermal efficiency reduction of only 2.21%, while yielding a considerable reduction in CO emissions by 27.05%, HC by 29.23%, and smoke opacity by 13.08%. NOx emissions increased moderately. This approach, integrating nano catalysis, AI-driven optimization, and practical engine testing, constitutes a promising pathway for clean energy advancement and sustainable transportation solutions.

title: Scalable physics-informed joint state-of-charge and state-of-health estimation framework toward real-time operation of multi-cell lithium-ion energy storage systems
abstract: Accurate estimation of battery internal states is essential for ensuring the safety and efficiency of multi-cell lithium-ion energy storage systems. However, strong coupling between state-of-charge and state-of-health, together with degradation dynamics and inter-cell variability, makes reliable joint estimation challenging under practical operating conditions. It is hypothesized that integrating degradation-aware modeling and inter-cell consistency learning within a unified framework can improve joint estimation performance. A scalable physics-informed joint estimation framework is developed, combining a multi-scale tensor neural operator for degradation modeling, a dynamic graph attention mechanism for inter-cell interaction learning, and a physics-augmented extended Kalman filter for real-time state correction. Experimental results on a laboratory dataset demonstrate improved performance compared with representative baseline methods, achieving a state-of-charge mean absolute error of 0.6% and a state-of-health mean absolute error of 1.1%, with inference latency below 10 ms per cycle. Validation is conducted under controlled laboratory settings with synthetically constructed multi-cell configurations, and real-world field validation, cross-chemistry generalization, and embedded system implementation are not included; therefore, the proposed approach provides a methodological foundation with potential applicability to battery management systems.

title: Safe reinforcement learning-based speed scheduling for an unmanned photovoltaic-battery vessel under uncertainties of solar irradiance and sea waves
abstract: Unmanned photovoltaic (PV)-battery vessels offer a zero-carbon and sustainable solution for long-voyage offshore tasks like measurement and survey. However, uncertainties of solar irradiance intermittency and wave height fluctuation challenge the speed scheduling to maintain an uninterrupted power supply during long-voyage tasks. Reinforcement learning (RL) excels in such sequential decision-making with uncertainties, but lacks an explicit mechanism to enforce safety constraints for uninterrupted power supply. Robust model predictive control (RMPC) addresses safety constraints, but struggles with nonlinear dynamics and nonconvexity. To tackle this issue, this paper develops a safe RL framework by combining RL to extend voyage, with the robust method as a safety filter to adjust RL action for safety. However, the conventional RMPC adopting the worst-case scenario in the whole prediction horizon may overly constrain the RL actions. A modified RMPC (mRMPC) is proposed to balance safety guarantees and reduced limits on actions. The mRMPC segments the prediction horizon into a short receding one, adopting the worst-case scenario, and a long shrinking one, employing a less severe scenario. Moreover, an action modification penalty is introduced in the reward function to improve exploration efficiency. Simulation results demonstrate the superior safety and voyage extension performance of the proposed method. Sensitivity analysis shows that combining a 6-hour short receding horizon with a 99% severe scenario in the long shrinking horizon outperforms other combinations in safety and voyage performance. The action modification penalty improves voyage optimality and reduces 30% training time. Robustness of the proposed method to modeling mismatches is also examined.

title: Physics-informed hybrid Digital Twin for decoupling multi-source degradation in marine propulsion systems
abstract: Accurate degradation quantification in marine propulsion systems is essential for restoring optimal energy conversion efficiency and advancing intelligent condition-based maintenance. However, real-time onboard diagnosis is severely restricted by limited sensor availability. Under such constraints, multiple concurrent aging mechanisms produce nearly identical macroscopic outputs, causing inverse identification to suffer from structural equifinality. Furthermore, conventional metaheuristic solvers and Bayesian inference methods demand prohibitive computational costs and yield inaccurate estimations. To overcome these bottlenecks, this study proposes a physics-informed framework termed Sequential Two-stage Reconstruction for Inverse Degradation Estimation (STRIDE). A fast Digital Twin is constructed via a hybrid methodology superimposing global polynomial regression with a local Radial Basis Function network. Crucially, STRIDE exploits single-cylinder motoring conditions to isolate air-path degradation. These initial estimates subsequently serve as Tikhonov-regularized priors for fuel-path reconstruction under normal firing operations. This sequential strategy systematically transforms one ill-conditioned six-parameter inverse problem into two well-conditioned subproblems without requiring extra physical sensors. Validation across 100 stochastic multi-fault scenarios demonstrates exceptional precision, accurately quantifying coupled degradation with minimal root mean square errors, including 0.011 °CA for injection timing and 1.771 mg/cyc for fuel mass. Extensive benchmarking confirms that the proposed framework significantly outperforms traditional optimization algorithms and advanced probabilistic baselines in decoupling accuracy. Deployed on a real-time Hardware-in-the-Loop simulator, the complete diagnostic cycle executes in approximately 15 ms. By successfully decoupling multi-source degradation and mathematically circumventing structural equifinality, this architecture establishes a highly accurate and computationally feasible foundation for dynamic efficiency recovery in aging marine power systems.

title: Physics-Informed neural networks with resnet-based two-stage training for transient multi-domain wellbore temperature prediction in deep drilling
abstract: Accurate prediction of transient wellbore temperature evolution in deep and ultra-deep wells under extreme high-temperature and high-pressure conditions is critical for ensuring drilling safety and optimizing thermal management. Conventional grid-based numerical simulations are computationally expensive, whereas purely data-driven surrogate models are prone to losing physical fidelity and global generalization capability when only sparse observations are available. To overcome these limitations, this study proposes an improved physics-informed neural network architecture for transient multi-domain coupled heat-transfer dynamics in the drill string–annulus–formation system. The proposed framework innovatively integrates a two-stage training strategy progressing from data fitting to physics correction, a residual-connection-based dual-branch mapping structure, and an adaptive loss-gradient penalty mechanism, thereby effectively mitigating convergence stiffness and gradient pathologies during the optimization of strongly coupled multi-scale heat-transfer equations. The governing partial differential equations and their initial and boundary conditions are seamlessly embedded into the loss function, which anchors the model to sparse field measurements while strictly maintaining global thermodynamic consistency. Multi-dimensional benchmark tests and comparisons with field measurements demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves excellent predictive fidelity, with the root mean square error at key monitoring points consistently below 1.8 °C and the maximum relative error strictly controlled within 2.3%. More importantly, compared with the conventional finite difference method, the proposed model achieves an approximately two-order-of-magnitude improvement in computational efficiency under GPU acceleration, requiring only seconds for a single forward inference and thus exhibiting strong potential for real-time engineering assessment. Combined with interpretability-based attribution analysis, the model further quantitatively reveals the dominant physical roles of fluid specific heat capacity and circulation time in governing bottom-hole temperature evolution. Owing to its rigorous physics-constrained learning mechanism and excellent computational robustness, the proposed framework can be broadly extended to digital-twin modeling of complex subsurface transient multi-domain heat-transfer processes, including geothermal exploitation and deep-Earth exploration.

title: Performance and uniformity enhancement in low‑platinum PEMFCs via synergistic dual‑segment power‑law platinum and ionomer gradients: A physics‑informed multi‑objective optimization approach
abstract: Low platinum loading severely restricts the performance and durability of proton exchange membrane fuel cells (PEMFCs). To overcome this, a physics-informed analysis and optimization framework is proposed to condense high-dimensional distribution spaces into interpretable parameters for efficient gradient cathode catalyst layer (CCL) designs. Drawing on regional sensitivity analyses, a dual-segment power-law profile (DSPLP) is introduced to address region-specific demands for Pt and ionomer. A three-dimensional multiphase PEMFC model with agglomerate submodel evaluates net output power and current density uniformity across DSPLP configurations. Independent and interactive DSPLP-based Pt loading and ionomer-to-carbon (I/C) ratio distributions are sequentially analyzed to identify critical parameters and influencing mechanisms, followed by multi-objective optimization for synergistic Pt-ionomer designs. Results show that compared to linear distribution, independent DSPLP-based Pt and ionomer gradients primarily mitigate ohmic and concentration losses, respectively, boosting net performance. However, both degrade current density uniformity by modulating proton availability and oxygen transport resistance, particularly steep ionomer gradients. The Pt-ionomer gradient interaction flattens the optimal Pt distribution to near-linear and lowers the mean I/C ratio from 0.70 to 0.60. Ultimately, at a Pt loading of 0.1 mg·cm−2, the optimized DSPLP CCL reduces concentration loss by 0.04 V via ionomer gradient, supplemented by Pt-driven ohmic mitigation, yielding a 5.26% increase in peak net power over uniform CCL, exceeding the 3.52% gain from linear CCL. Synergistic effects further suppress extreme local current zones, improving uniformity by 5.65% at 1.5 A·cm−2. This work provides a broadly applicable approach and valuable insights to support membrane electrode assembly design for next-generation PEMFCs.

title: Hybrid machine learning–NSGA-II optimization framework for biogas-based multigeneration systems: thermodynamic and economic performance enhancement
abstract: Addressing global energy and freshwater demands requires efficient renewable-based polygeneration technologies. This study proposes and optimizes a biogas-fueled multigeneration system for electricity generation, freshwater, hydrogen, and heating. A comprehensive thermodynamic and exergoeconomic model is initially created via Engineering Equation Solver (EES) to assess the performance of the system. To overcome the computational barriers of iterative simulations, a cutting-edge hybrid machine learning (ML) framework is developed in Python. This framework employs a weighted ensemble of Multilayer Perceptron (MLP) and Extra Trees (ET) algorithms as a precise surrogate model, mapping the interactions between five key decision variables (air preheater temperature (T3), gas turbine inlet temperature (T4), air compressor pressure ratio (PRac), evaporator temperature (Tev)), and performance metrics with exceptional accuracy (R2 > 0.99). It is revealed from sensitivity analysis that the gas turbine inlet temperature (T4) is the dominant parameter, significantly influencing both thermodynamic efficiency and economic feasibility. Subsequently, the surrogate model is coupled with the NSGA-II algorithm for multi-objective optimization. To ensure a robust selection of the final design, two Multi-Criteria Decision Making (MCDM) methods, TOPSIS and VIKOR, were employed. The TOPSIS method identified an optimal configuration yielding an energy efficiency of 77.76%, an exergy efficiency of 30.99%, and a unit product cost of 29.58$/GJ In comparison VIKOR proposed a solution with a minimized cost of 28.98$/GJ and a higher exergy efficiency of 31.90%, offering flexible trade-offs for decision-makers. Final validation confirms the model’s reliability, with hybrid ML-predicted values showing a relative error of less than 0.8%. This study demonstrates that the proposed ML-assisted framework offers a computationally efficient pathway for the sustainable design of biomass-driven energy systems.

title: Machine learning framework for integrated catalyst-process modelling for direct conversion of CO2 to dimethyl ether
abstract: Energy and environmental sustainability are vital for global development. The use of fossil fuels has advanced civilization but has caused significant CO2 emissions. Alternative pathways are essential to meet the rising energy demands sustainably. In this context, the direct catalytic hydrogenation of CO2 to dimethyl ether offers a promising route for carbon mitigation and clean energy production. Despite its abundance, the activation of CO2 remains challenging because of its thermodynamic stability and kinetic inertness, leading to low conversion rates and limited DME yields. Traditional trial-and-error experiments to overcome these barriers are resource intensive and time consuming. This study proposes a machine learning (ML) framework to elucidate the relationship between catalyst composition and operating conditions on CO2 conversion and product selectivity, enabling predictive modelling of direct catalytic CO2-to-DME performance. A diverse experimental dataset comprising 16 input features was compiled to predict the CO2 conversion and selectivity of DME, Methanol and CO. Multiple machine learning algorithms spanning linear to nonlinear models were trained using 5-fold cross-validation, with hyperparameter optimization and performance evaluation based on the Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) and coefficient of determination (R2). The Gradient Boosted Regression Tree (GBRT) model achieved the highest predictive accuracy, with R2 values of 0.92 and 0.94 (test data) for CO2 conversion and DME selectivity, respectively. Feature importance and partial dependence plot analyses were employed to elucidate the influence of individual features and their interdependencies on governing catalyst activity. Overall, this study highlights the potential of ML to overcome the complexities of bifunctional catalyst systems and offers actionable insights for enhancing the efficiency and sustainability of direct CO2 to DME conversion processes.

title: Artificial intelligence assisted framework for techno economic optimization and reliability enhancement of standalone photovoltaic systems
abstract: Solar photovoltaic (PV) energy is a suitable choice for sustainable and decentralized electricity production, especially in areas where extending the grid is either technically difficult or financially challenged. However, solar resources are intermittent, load demand fluctuates and battery performance is uncertain. In view of this, a study has been proposed to develop a MATLAB based framework for the optimal design and techno-economic assessment of standalone PV systems. The proposed approach integrates analytical modelling, particle swarm optimization (PSO), and artificial neural network (ANN) based surrogate prediction within the integrated sizing framework. System reliability is evaluated using loss of power supply probability (LPSP) by considering solar irradiance, temperature, battery state of charge (SoC) and energy balance under the implemented modelling assumptions. In addition, diminishing return effect (DRE) is used to observe how variations in PV and battery capacities influence system cost and reliability improvement, thereby identifying regions where additional capacity produces progressively smaller reliability benefits. This framework is evaluated using meteorological data for Chennai, India. Under the chosen design and operating conditions, the optimized system achieves an LPSP of 0.0206, corresponding to approximately 97.94 % supply reliability, with a levelized cost of electricity (LCOE) of approximately $0.13/kWh. The ANN surrogate, trained using analytical and PSO generated sizing samples achieves R ≈ 0.99 within the evaluated dataset, indicating close contract between the surrogate predictions target sizing outputs and supporting rapid sizing estimation within the selected design domain. The results demonstrate the potential of the integrated framework as a decision support approach for equally examining component sizing, economic performance, reliability and surrogate ANN based estimation in standalone PV system development.

title: A Sobolev-constrained Fourier neural operator for high-throughput thermoelectric device screening
abstract: High-throughput thermoelectric screening requires device-level evaluation across large material libraries, but repeatedly solving the coupled finite-current fields is computationally expensive. Here, we develop a Sobolev-constrained Fourier neural operator (Sobolev-FNO) that reconstructs the temperature and electric-potential fields. Current density, load power, total hot-side heat input, and conversion efficiency are then evaluated consistently from these fields at the same matched-load operating state. The model is trained on 9145 physically audited FEM cases incorporating finite-current thermoelectric coupling and temperature-dependent transport properties. Its objective combines field reconstruction with gradient, boundary, and thermoelectric heat-flux constraints to improve derivative-sensitive device quantities. Formula-grouped partitioning prevents exact chemical-formula overlap among data subsets, while two complete material families are withheld for out-of-distribution evaluation. The median relative efficiency error is 0.143% on the test set and 0.269% for the withheld families. Ablation and common-data baseline comparisons support the contribution of derivative-aware supervision. The end-to-end evaluation requires about 2.900 ms per case, approximately 2292 times faster than the nonlinear FEM workflow. The resulting Sobolev-FNO provides an efficient screen–then–confirm framework for material prioritization across large-scale thermoelectric material libraries.

title: Hybrid physics-informed and data-driven modeling of material–process–property relationships in extrusion-printed GelMA/alginate vascular scaffolds
abstract: Three-dimensional (3D) printing has enabled the fabrication of hydrogel-based vascular scaffolds with tubular geometries. However, precision engineering of these scaffolds remains a critical challenge because of the unclear relationships among materials, processing parameters, and final structural properties. To address this, a novel integrated physics-informed and data-driven framework that unifies process prediction, interpretable composition–mechanics modeling, and surrogate-based formulation optimization with experimental verification was proposed, thereby reducing reliance on trial-and-error screening under limited experimental sampling. Specifically, tunable bioinks were bioprinted through a 22 G conical nozzle, followed by quantitative characterization of structural fidelity through wall thickness measurements. To capture extrusion physics, a physics-informed neural network (PINN) combining a closed-form conical-nozzle pressure model with two learnable corrections accurately predicts required pressure across compositions and print speeds while enforcing physical plausibility, offering an early demonstration of PINN methodology in bioprinting. Uniaxial tests revealed vertical–circumferential anisotropy, with Young’s modulus and ultimate tensile strain varying with composition. Besides, beyond black-box fitting, symbolic regression produced compact, interpretable relations between composition and directional mechanics, showing strong agreement with experimental measurements. Gaussian process and random forest regressors mapped bulk mechanical response to composition and enabled optimization, identifying distinct optima: 16.58% GelMA/5.10% alginate for superior vertical performance and 10.96% GelMA/4.02% alginate for superior circumferential performance. Experimental validation showed < 8% deviation between predictions and measurements. Additionally, cyclic tensile tests exhibited overlapping strain-stress curves, indicating dynamic stability of printed structures with optimized compositions. Standard cell-viability assays supported the preliminary cytocompatibility of the optimized bioinks and printing conditions.

title: Artificial Intelligence as Multifaceted Toolkit for Antibacterial Drug Discovery against Resistance
abstract: How artificial intelligence (AI) can be rationally applied to antibacterial drug discovery and development to overcome antimicrobial resistance (AMR) remains insufficiently defined, particularly across different resistance mechanisms and translational stages. The global emergence and dissemination of AMR are compromising conventional antibacterial therapies, while slow antibiotic discovery, limited target diversity, and reliance on single-mechanism drug design further increase the risk of inadequate treatment options. With strengths in multi-omics integration, complex pattern recognition, and structure-guided molecular design, AI offers a promising approach to support next-generation antibacterial development. This review focuses on AI-related strategies for antimicrobial development against bacterial resistance and provides a systematic overview of advances in target identification, molecular design, activity prediction, and clinical translation. Rather than proposing a new theoretical framework, the review introduces a pragmatic synthesis tool for evaluating where AI adds value and where important limitations remain, considering application objectives, data properties, validation depth, biological interpretability, and translational feasibility. Major challenges are highlighted, including data heterogeneity, clonal bias, limited external validation, discrepancies between in vitro activity and in vivo therapeutic efficacy, and the absence of regulatory approval for any AI-discovered or AI-designed antibacterial agent. Correspondingly, future directions are delineated, including multimodal data integration, explainable AI methodologies, validation through synthetic biology, and coordinated international regulatory efforts. Overall, this review provides a structured overview of how AI can be integrated with rational antibacterial design while considering both its potential and current limitations for addressing multidrug-resistant pathogens.

title: Machine learning-driven customizable mechanical design of diamond plate lattice metamaterials
abstract: This study presents a machine-learning, multi-objective inverse-design framework that couples an XGBoost surrogate with NSGA-II to tailor the mechanical performance of diamond-based plate-lattice (DM) metamaterials. Trained on finite-element (FE) simulations of 316 L stainless-steel lattices, the curve-driven surrogate predicts the full compressive stress–strain response across a broad geometric design space without manual feature engineering. Compared with conventional regressors, it cuts prediction error by >96% and raises R2 to 0.994. When integrated with NSGA-II, the framework jointly optimizes specific energy absorption (SEA), specific plateau strength (SPS), and specific stiffness (SE) with explicit trade-off control, producing lattice designs that simultaneously enhance strength and energy absorption; the composite weighted error for multi-objective customization remains <10% relative to FE benchmarks. Bayesian hyperparameter tuning further extends the surrogate’s reliable prediction range in relative density by 107% (from 0.12 to 0.53 to 0.092–0.94), demonstrating extrapolation across a wider density span. Overall, the XGBoost–NSGA-II framework is robust and practical, offering an efficient route to engineer plate-lattice metamaterials with tailored stiffness, strength, and energy absorption, while accelerating their deployment in lightweight applications.

title: Sensitivity-analysis guided Bayesian optimization for crystal plasticity parameter identification
abstract: Twinning-induced plasticity (TWIP) is a crucial deformation mechanism in many alloys directly linked with their ductility. In addition to experimental approaches, crystal plasticity (CP) modeling is another handy way to study TWIP. Nevertheless, reliable determination of the parameters of complex CP models imposes a first challenge prior to any meaningful modeling practices. In the present work, we crafted a framework for efficiently and robustly determining the parameters of CP models. The novelty of the framework lies in combining the Sobol sensitivity analysis and Bayesian optimization in sequence, where the former is for reducing the dimension of the input parameters followed by the latter to find the values of a shrunk set of parameters. The robustness and accuracy of the framework were demonstrated with three case studies of varying complexities where CP models with varied considerations of twinning and for three typical metallic crystal structures, namely, face-centered cubic (FCC), body-centered cubic (BCC), and hexagonal close-packed (HCP) were accounted for. Compared to alternatives, our framework is capable of pinpointing a smaller optimization objective, making it both robust and efficient in identifying the parameters of CP models. The efficient and robust determination of CP model parameters with the proposed framework set the foundation for in-depth investigations of deformation mechanisms involving twinning, dislocation, etc.

title: Physics-informed data-driven constitutive modeling of compressible, nonlinear soft materials under multiaxial cyclic loading
abstract: Modeling nonlinear, history-dependent viscoelastic behavior under multiaxial cyclic loading remains challenging because existing approaches address only parts of the problem. Purely data-driven models can learn time-dependent responses but often require large datasets, lack interpretability, and may violate physical constraints. Conversely, regression-based surrogates, including GPR and polynomial models, efficiently capture smooth equilibrium behavior but cannot represent path dependence or long-term memory effects. Existing hybrid models typically combine neural networks with physics-based constraints, yet they rarely integrate separate surrogates for equilibrium and nonequilibrium responses within a unified constitutive framework, nor do they enforce objectivity, material symmetry, and thermodynamic consistency at all stages. To address this gap, we propose a physics-informed hybrid framework in which GPR learns the smooth volumetric and isochoric equilibrium response, while RNN–LSTM networks capture the history-dependent viscoelastic contribution. The stress is decomposed into volumetric, isochoric hyperelastic, and isochoric viscoelastic components, each treated with its own surrogate and trained under explicit physical constraints. Training data are generated using the nonlinear Holzapfel differential viscoelastic model, and both short-term and long-term datasets are constructed to span distinct memory behaviors. The framework is evaluated under diverse multiaxial loading paths, including variable stretch ratios, multiple strain rates, and both tension and compression, with additional tests conducted beyond the training domain. The results show that the hybrid surrogate preserves objectivity, material symmetry, and thermodynamic admissibility while accurately reproducing nonlinear, rate-dependent, and history-sensitive behavior.

title: Machine learning based inverse design of variable stiffness mechanical metamaterials
abstract: Materials with tailored variable-stiffness mechanical responses are pivotal for innovations in adaptive structural design. However, the high-dimensional non-linearity and complex coupling of their deformation mechanisms pose significant barriers to efficient inverse design. Here, we propose a novel machine learning-powered inverse design framework utilizing curved beams to realize programmable variable stiffness mechanical metamaterials. In the proposed design framework, it is first shown that the mechanical response of unit cells can be broadly tuned by designing the geometric configuration of curved beams. A data-driven machine learning pipeline is then developed to efficiently tailor unit cells with targeted mechanical properties via inverse design. By precisely programming the deformation coupling behavior of unit cells and implementing multistage stiffness modulation, variable stiffness characteristics are endowed to macroscopic metamaterials. The validation results based on the dataset demonstrate that the accuracy of the predicted mechanical response generated through machine learning reached 96.89%, and the variable stiffness metamaterial constructed from these unit cells achieved the expected performance in both simulation and experiment. Finally, a new type of airless wheel with variable stiffness is developed using the proposed design framework, and its superior environmental adaptability compared to conventional airless wheels is validated through dynamic analysis. The proposed inverse design framework can potentially be extended to other nonlinear mechanical response scenarios, enabling predictable and intelligent structural designs.

title: Contact-based high-throughput material characterization via Kolmogorov-Arnold Transformer neural operator
abstract: High-throughput characterization (HTC) techniques grounded in contact mechanics have significantly propelled advancements in materials science by enabling quantitative assessments of material properties efficiently and precisely. Tailored for HTC of whole-field material properties, an effective Kolmogorov-Arnold Transformer neural operator (KATNO) architecture is established to conduct the inverse contact analysis, where the datasets are prepared through finite element analysis of isotropic inhomogeneous cubes as well as symplectic analysis of layered cylinders. The normalized cross-attention and self-attention modules are designed to evaluate queries, keys, and values within the Transformer framework. Additionally, a gating network is employed to average the weights of multiple expert group-rational Kolmogorov-Arnold networks (GR-KANs). In representative numerical examples, predicted results and ground truth exhibit high consistency. Various KATNO architectures are explored to identify essential design criteria according to the mean L2 relative error. The limitations of neural operators based on contact analysis are highlighted, offering insights for future advancements in HTC techniques.

title: A physics-informed hybrid model for grinding force prediction
abstract: Accurate prediction of grinding force is crucial for enhancing machining precision. Existing models often rely on simplified assumptions of rigid abrasive grains or mean chip thickness, neglecting the dynamic coupling between wheel surface randomness and grain wear. This paper proposes a physics-informed hybrid grinding force model (PHGFM). By integrating the geometric characteristics and wear behavior of grains, the wheel topography is reconstructed to accurately capture the evolution of the wheel surface topography during grinding. Furthermore, a novel undeformed chip thickness (UCT) model is proposed based on kinematic analysis and dynamic height distribution of grains. Moreover, the physical force computations are embedded into a physics-informed neural network (PINN), where a hybrid loss function incorporating both physical constraints and data-driven components is designed to achieve synergistic optimization of physics priors and data features. The proposed hybrid model demonstrates high predictive accuracy for grinding forces in brittle materials such as SiC ceramics under various grinding conditions. The average prediction errors for the normal and tangential grinding forces are 6.76 % and 7.28 %, respectively, while the minimum errors for the normal and tangential forces reach 3.35 % and 5.70 %, respectively.

title: A novel physics-informed neural network via field mapping
abstract: Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) have emerged as a promising tool for solving forward and inverse problems governed by partial differential equations (PDEs). However, existing PINNs rely on point-to-point functional mapping and struggle to meet the challenges of efficiency and accuracy of solving PDEs, especially in the presence of sharply varying physical fields. To address these issues, we propose a novel physics-driven framework based on a learning philosophy involving spatio-temporal field input and physical field output, namely physical field neural network (PFNN). The improved input layer ingests physical information from all spatio-temporal coordinates for function mapping, and the enhanced output layer adopts an ultra-wide architecture, facilitating the learning of complex patterns. A numerical difference scheme is introduced to approximate the required derivatives, resolving the inconsistency between the dense Jacobian matrix resulting from chain-rule differentiation in the network and the theoretical independence of the PDE differential terms. A coordinate transformation module is integrated, allowing the numerical differentiation-based PFNN to learn PDEs over irregular physical domains. The PFNN not only effectively addresses high-frequency and multi-scale challenges in the Helmholtz equation and heat conduction equation, but also reliably solves the sharply varying stress and electric potential and temperature fields in the elastic equilibrium equation and thermo-electro coupling equation. Moreover, the PFNN demonstrates strong robustness in parameter identification for the thermos-electric coupling equation under noisy conditions. Compared to traditional PINNs, the PFNN achieves a maximum error decrease of three orders of magnitude and a speed increase of up to 2257%. With reference to the deep energy method (DEM) and PINN with Fourier features (FF-PINN), the PFNN delivers at least 180% and 61% higher precision, as well as 249% and 4082% faster speed. Relative to the Kolmogorov-Arnold-Informed Neural Network (KINN), the PFNN improves speed by 609% while maintaining similar high precision. The proposed PFNN offers notable advantages in accuracy, efficiency, robustness, and generality, providing a valuable reference to the field of AI for PDEs.

title: Physics-informed deep operator network for formability evaluation of dual-phase steels
abstract: Developing a robust computational method for formability assessment is essential to ensure stability and integrity in industrial metal-forming processes. This study targets the integration of the merits of physics-informed and deep learning neural networks for this issue. Specifically, a configuration strategy is proposed to construct a framework that satisfies both mechanical and computational requirements for predicting forming limits. First, we proposed a novel physics-informed neural implicit flow (PINIF) architecture that hierarchically decomposed the complexities of crystal plasticity deformation into three nested neural networks, ShapeNet, CrystalNet, and DeformNet, that addressed spatial, crystalline, and strain-path-dependent complexities, respectively. PINIF enabled a robust representation of the accommodation capability for plastic deformation in dual-phase (DP) steels under multipath loading, reflecting the mechanical aspects of formability assessments that involved microstructure and multipath dependence. Within PINIF, CrystalNet played a pivotal role by embedding the crystalline characteristics of DP steels to enable adaptive responses to multipath-dependent behaviors, as evidenced by comparisons with benchmark crystal plasticity simulations. Building on this capability, a deep operator network (DeepONet) was further developed to assess formability by repurposing frozen CrystalNet as a material-aware operator. This strategy eliminated redundant computational procedures and allowed a direct mapping from crystalline properties to forming limits. Furthermore, a measurement-informed loss was incorporated to enhance the physical fidelity of DeepONet. The proposed framework was validated using experimental data from formability tests of actual DP steels, demonstrating its efficacy and superiority. Finally, an analysis was conducted to provide physical insight into the influence of the material microstructure on formability.

title: Hybrid multilayer perceptron-convolutional neural network model for non-iterative topology optimization of 2D chiral metamaterials with shear-shear coupling
abstract: Optimizing chiral metamaterials with tailored mechanical coupling properties has been challenging, as conventional topology optimization (TO) methods require extensive iterative computations to achieve targeted mechanical coupling capabilities and chiral material symmetries along with sufficient bulk and shear stiffnesses. In this study, a hybrid multilayer perceptron (MLP)-convolutional neural network (CNN) model is developed for non-iterative, real-time TO of two-dimensional (2D) chiral metamaterials with shear-shear coupling capabilities at a significantly reduced computational cost. The newly proposed MLP-CNN model integrates an MLP encoder, which processes only three scalar design parameters, with a CNN decoder that directly generates the optimal chiral layouts. Trained on a comprehensive dataset covering the admissible design space of right-handed and left-handed chiral metamaterials, the new hybrid MLP-CNN model accurately reproduces optimal layouts and mechanical coupling properties predicted by the traditional TO method with root-mean-square errors below 1% while achieving a 99.8% reduction in inference time. A distinctive advantage of the proposed model is its ability to process scalar inputs directly, thereby eliminating the need for image-based input encoding typical of existing deep learning TO models. The hybrid MLP-CNN model provides a generic and efficient paradigm for real-time, data-driven TO of chiral metamaterials.

title: Synergistic crystal plasticity and machine learning unraveling TSV-Cu fatigue
abstract: Thermally induced copper (Cu) protrusion in through-silicon vias (TSVs) represents a critical thermo-mechanical reliability challenge in three-dimensional integrated systems. To resolve the roles of crystallographic anisotropy and microstructural geometry, an integrated framework combining physics-based crystal plasticity finite element modeling and data-driven machine learning was developed in this study. Ex-situ electron backscatter diffraction measurements demonstrated that the macroscopic grain network remained statistically invariant during low-ΔT thermal cycling. This observation justified the assumption of a non-evolving microstructure in the simulations. The crystal plasticity results indicated that non-uniform protrusion originated from strain incompatibility driven by Schmid-factor mismatch between neighboring grains. Due to idealized boundary conditions, the model underestimated the absolute stress level. However, it accurately reproduced the normalized protrusion kinetics and predicted the onset of interfacial cracking near the sidewall at approximately 20 cycles. Machine-learning analysis further identified grain size as the most influential statistical descriptor among the considered single-grain features. From a mechanistic perspective, grain size did not replace crystallographic effects but served as a geometric proxy reflecting boundary density and local mechanical constraints. Together, these results established a hierarchical failure mechanism in TSV-Cu, where crystallographic anisotropy governed the initiation of strain incompatibility, while the geometric microstructural network controlled the intensity and spatial localization of damage.

title: Physics-informed ultrasonic SVM for coating interfacial stiffness evaluation
abstract: Precise characterization of interfacial bonding strength in coated structures is critical for structural integrity but remains challenging due to the complex interference patterns caused by multiple internal reflections. These reflections generate "pseudo-notches" in the ultrasonic spectrum, rendering traditional amplitude-based or simple resonance-tracking methods ineffective. To address this challenge, we propose a physics-informed machine learning framework for the inverse determination of interfacial contact stiffness. A Phase-Amplitude Matching (PAM) mechanism is introduced, utilizing the frequency-domain conjugate differentiation method to construct a Phase Derivative Spectrum (PDS), which enhances the detectability of abrupt phase variation at authentic resonance points. Through the integration of PDS intensity with spectral morphological features, a multidimensional feature space is constructed to train a Support Vector Machine (SVM) classifier using a finite element simulation dataset. Furthermore, a novel quantitative index, Normalized Notch Offset (NNO), is established to decouple bonding quality from thickness variations. Experimental results on aluminum and epoxy coatings with controlled interfacial roughness demonstrate that the proposed method achieves a notch recognition accuracy of 96.5%. The extracted NNO index exhibits a strong monotonic correlation with interfacial stiffness and maintains high robustness (deviation <10%) against coating thickness fluctuations. This approach provides a reliable, baseline-free solution for the quantitative evaluation of coating bonding quality in complex interference environments.

title: Deep learning-driven inverse design of TPMS lattice sandwich structure
abstract: In aerospace components, the optimization design of the triply periodic minimal surface (TPMS) lattice structure encounters issues of unified parameterization for discrete design variables and multiphysics coupling. A deep learning-driven multiobjective inverse optimization design framework for lightweight TPMS lattice structures with targeted thermal insulation and load-bearing performances was proposed in this study to circumvent non-differentiability challenges inherent in transitions across different unit cell types. Functionally graded TPMS lattice structures with adjustable structural parameters were constructed, and the coupled thermal-fluid-mechanical finite element analyses were performed to estimate their corresponding thermal and mechanical performances. A back propagation neural network (BPNN) was established as a surrogate model to capture the relationship between structural parameters and the resulting thermo-mechanical properties. The BPNN model was then integrated with the genetic algorithm (GA) for inverse design targeting required structural, thermal, and mechanical characteristics within discrete-continuous mixed design spaces. An adaptive dataset expansion (ADE) strategy was developed to generate a “deep learning - inverse design - coupled analysis” closed-loop error feedback system. Key findings revealed that the presented BPNN-GA framework achieves high accuracy (error: ∼1%) in the multi-objective inverse optimization design of TPMS lattice sandwich structures under multiphysics coupling scenarios. The thermomechanical performances of the designed structure were further validated through thermal-fluid coupling tests. This study establishes a transferable closed-loop framework that bridges deep learning surrogate modeling with multiphysics-coupled inverse optimization design, enabling simultaneous targeting of thermal, mechanical, and structural requirements, thereby offering practical pathways for thermomechanical protection components in lightweight aerospace structures.

title: Local balance for energy-based physics-informed neural networks on phase-field models
abstract: Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) based on energy minimization have emerged as a powerful framework for solving problems governed by convex energy functionals. However, their extension to phase-field models, which are characterized by non-convex energy functionals, often fails to yield nontrivial or physically valid steady-state solutions. While local constraints have been integrated to improve accuracy in convex settings, their role in energy-based PINNs for phase-field models has remained unclear. This work reveals that for phase-field models, fulfilling the steady-state form of local balance is not merely beneficial but necessary. By confining solutions to a physically admissible space, this fulfillment releases the physically relevant local minima from the strong pull of either the temporal inertia or latent global energy minimum. This mechanism is illustrated through several benchmarks. The release from the temporal inertia is demonstrated via two examples of standalone phase-field equations, where the steady states are path-dependent. The escape from the latent global energy minimum is manifested by an example of the multiphysics phase-field model for ferroelectric microstructures, where the steady states are path-independent. This insight also enables a refined energy-based PINN to directly obtain the steady state of a phase-field model. Thus, this work provides a step towards extending energy-based PINNs to broader classes of complex non-convex problems.

title: Physics-informed temporal convolutional networks for composite constitutive modeling
abstract: We propose a physics-informed temporal convolutional network (PITCN) framework for efficient constitutive modelling of composite materials under random loading paths. The core contributions lie in the effective integration of a temporal convolutional network to encode the historical stress-strain sequence into a material state vector, which is subsequently mapped by a fully connected network to approximate the free energy function. The constitutive relations are then derived via automatic differentiation. To ensure thermodynamic consistency under irreversible deformation, the non-negativity of both the free energy and the dissipation energy is enforced through penalty terms in the loss function. A key advantage of the PITCN framework is that it achieves high predictive accuracy without requiring experimentally inaccessible free energy or internal state variables during training. The method is efficiently integrated into ABAQUS through a user material subroutine, enabling seamless coupling with finite element solvers. The performance of the proposed PITCN is systematically evaluated at the material point level and in structural simulations under arbitrary loading/unloading conditions against conventional multiscale techniques, and is further validated against experimental measurements. Compared with conventional multiscale techniques, the PITCN achieves a speed-up of 19 times and a memory reduction of 107 times in structural applications, while maintaining comparable accuracy.

title: Physics-informed neural network for spectrum design in delayed vibration control
abstract: Time-delay coupling complicates spectrum design and stability-constrained optimization in active vibration control (AVC) systems, owing to infinite-dimensional dynamics and costly eigenvalue analysis. To address this problem, a physics-informed neural network is developed for surrogate-assisted leading spectrum design of delayed AVC systems. At its core, a physics-constrained eigenvalue regression network (PCER-Net) is constructed by embedding the residual of the delayed characteristic equation into training, thereby improving physical consistency, convergence stability, and generalization relative to a purely data-driven network. Based on the trained PCER-Net, a unified framework is established for stability classification, stability maximization, spectral-constrained inverse design, and stability-margin-constrained anti-resonance optimization. Experimental validation is performed on an active quasi-zero-stiffness (QZS) isolator with multiple delayed control structures, including single-delay feedback, dual-delay feedback, and hybrid feedforward-feedback configurations. In repeated optimization, the PCER-Net reduces the average task time from 14.53 s to 0.51 s for local optimization and from 351.22 s to 5.53 s for hybrid search, with break-even points reached after 116 and 6 tasks, respectively. Experimentally, the optimized hybrid controller achieves target transmissibility values of 0.2079 at 5 Hz and 0.1884 at 8 Hz, corresponding to 85.98% and 92.14% reductions relative to the passive QZS case.

title: Deep learning-driven multi-scale optimization for high-performance TPMS-based piezoelectric metamaterials
abstract: Advances in additive manufacturing of piezoelectric materials have highlighted the topology optimization of triply periodic minimal surface (TPMS)-based metamaterials as a critical frontier for next-generation sensors and actuators. However, topology optimization design of these materials has largely been restricted to single-scale or 2D models due to the prohibitive computational cost arising from complex cross-scale electromechanical coupling. To address this issue, we present a multi-scale topology optimization framework centered on a data-efficient deep learning surrogate model for TPMS-based piezoelectric metamaterials. This surrogate model rapidly predicts the effective properties of TPMS microstructures, enabling efficient multi-scale optimization for practical applications. Our framework allows for the simultaneous optimization of lattice density and piezoelectric polarization directions across arbitrary 3D macroscopic geometries. Numerical results demonstrate that this concurrent optimization strategy yields a 156.1% enhancement in output displacement for the TPMS-based actuator compared to the conventional one with uniform density and symmetrical polarization. This multi-scale topology optimization framework establishes a feasible and efficient pathway to unlock the full design potential of high-performance, architected piezoelectric metamaterials and devices.
